CSE470Software Engineering

Refactoring — one program, seven smells

A working semester-fee program that nobody would want to maintain. It compiles, it runs, and it prints eight lines that must not change. Your job is to find every code smell, name the Fowler refactoring that removes it, and apply them one at a time without ever breaking the output. The same program is given in Python and Java; both print exactly the same thing.

The program

FeeSystem bills one student for one semester. A RegularStudent has credits, a program, a waiver, an attendance range and a list of course fees. FeeMgr calculates the semester fee, FeeReport formats a summary line, and a VisitingStudent is billed by their home university instead.

That is the whole domain. Everything else wrong with the file is self-inflicted.

The output — this is your regression test

Spring 2026 1/1/2026 - 15/5/2026
40750.0
2950.0
Rafi | CSE | 12 cr | 56950.0
[800.0, 950.0, 1200.0]
[800.0, 950.0, 1200.0]
0

Eight lines. The eighth is blank: print(v.getTranscript()) prints an empty string. A diff will catch it even though your eye will not, which is the point of diffing rather than eyeballing.

Running it

python3 fee_system.py

javac -d out FeeSystem.java && java -cp out FeeSystem

Both files are self-contained and need nothing installed beyond a Python 3 interpreter and a JDK. Compile each Java program into its own directory — the problem and the solution declare classes of the same name, so sharing one output directory makes them overwrite each other.

The seven smells

1Inappropriate naming

Fowler's Mysterious Name — the cheapest smell to fix and the one that makes every other smell visible.

Naming

2Comments

Fowler calls comments a deodorant: they are often used to mask a smell rather than remove it.

Dispensables

3Long method

FeeMgr.calc is 48 lines and does six unrelated jobs. Its refactored replacement is 10.

Bloaters

4Long parameter list

calc takes eleven parameters. Four of them do not need to be parameters at all.

Bloaters

5Feature envy

RegularStudent is a bag of getters. Every calculation about a student happens somewhere else.

Couplers

6Duplicated code

All five levels of duplication are in this one program — and only one of them is visible to a copy-paste detector.

Dispensables

7Refused bequest

VisitingStudent inherits three methods and refuses all three. The hierarchy is asserting something that is not true.

OO abusers

Every one of those numbers moved without the output moving at all. That is the definition of refactoring.

How to use this page

Work through the smells in order — they are ordered by how safe they are to apply, not by how bad they are. Renaming first makes the rest visible.

Each smell page shows you where the smell is and asks you to fix it. The Reveal solution button — and the Solutions switch in the top bar — uncover the reference answer, with a before-and-after of the exact code. Write your own version first.

Every code block has Python and Java tabs. The two are the same refactoring, not the same code; where the languages genuinely disagree there is a Java notes panel saying so.

Because only one page is on screen at a time, find-in-page cannot see the rest. Type three or more characters in the filter box and it searches the full text of every page, code included.

Keyboard: / to filter, [ and ] for previous and next, l to flip the code language, s to toggle solutions. Printing gives you what is on screen — a clean worksheet with solutions hidden, a marking key with them shown.

How to work: baby steps and a regression test

Refactoring is not rewriting. The distinguishing feature is that you can stop at any moment and still have a working program.

Why the output is fixed

Refactoring means changing the internal structure of code without changing its observable behaviour. For this program, observable behaviour is exactly one thing: the eight lines it prints. Fix that as a contract first, and every edit afterwards has an objective pass/fail test.

Without that contract you are not refactoring, you are rewriting — and a rewrite that quietly changes a fee by 5% is indistinguishable from a successful refactoring until a student complains.

Set the regression test up first

# capture the golden output, once, before you touch anything
python3 fee_system.py > golden.txt
javac -d out FeeSystem.java && java -cp out FeeSystem > golden_java.txt
diff golden.txt golden_java.txt        # must be empty

# after every single edit, from now on
python3 fee_system.py | diff golden.txt -   # must print nothing

diff catches the trailing blank line, trailing spaces and 40750.0 versus 40750.00. Your eye does not. Run it after every step, not at the end.

The loop

  1. Pick one smell.
  2. Pick the smallest change that removes part of it — one rename, one extracted method. Not the whole smell; one step of it.
  3. Make the change.
  4. Run the program and diff against the golden file.
  5. If the diff is empty, commit. If it is not, undo — do not debug forward. The last step was wrong and it is two lines long, so throwing it away costs nothing.
  6. Go to step 2.

The commit after each green run is what makes the undo cheap. A student who refactors for forty minutes and then discovers the output changed has no way back; a student who commits nine times has eight.

The order that works

The seven smells in this exercise are deliberately ordered by risk:

  • Rename first (smell 1). It is mechanical, an editor can do it, and it makes every other smell legible.
  • Then extract (smells 2 and 3). Extracting a method cannot change behaviour if you move the lines unchanged and pass everything they use.
  • Then move (smells 4 and 5). Moving a method between classes is where signatures change, so it is where mistakes start.
  • Then merge duplicates (smell 6). Riskiest, because the copies are never quite identical — see the 0.0 versus "" return values.
  • Then fix the hierarchy (smell 7). Largest blast radius, so it goes last, when everything else is already clean and tested.

What “preserving behaviour” does and does not cover

Byte-identical stdout is the contract for this exercise. It is not the whole of observable behaviour in general, and this program contains a reminder: replacing the in-place sortFees with a function that returns a new list changes what a caller would see if it relied on the mutation. No caller here does, so the output is unchanged — but the behaviour is not quite. Real refactoring needs real tests, not just a printed transcript.

What to hand in

  • The refactored program, in whichever language you were assigned.
  • A table with one row per smell: the smell's name, where you found it, the Fowler refactoring you applied, and one sentence on why.
  • The diff output proving the program still prints the same eight lines.

"""
CSE 470 - Software Engineering
Refactoring Practice Problem (Python)

Semester Fee Processing System.

The program works. Do not change what it prints.
Your job is to find the code smells and refactor them away.
"""


class AttRange:
    def __init__(self, l, h):
        self.l = l
        self.h = h

    def getLow(self):
        return self.l

    def getHigh(self):
        return self.h


class AttPolicy:
    def withinRange(self, low, high):
        return low >= 60 and high <= 100


class Member:
    def __init__(self, i, n):
        self.i = i
        self.n = n

    def getId(self):
        return self.i

    def getName(self):
        return self.n

    def getScholarshipPercent(self):
        return 25

    def getTranscript(self):
        return "TRANSCRIPT OF " + self.n

    def payTuition(self, amt):
        print(self.n + " paid " + str(amt))


class RegularStudent(Member):
    def __init__(self, i, n, cr, p, w, a, f):
        super().__init__(i, n)
        self.cr = cr
        self.p = p
        self.w = w
        self.a = a
        self.f = f

    def getCredits(self):
        return self.cr

    def getProgram(self):
        return self.p

    def getWaiver(self):
        return self.w

    def getAtt(self):
        return self.a

    def getFees(self):
        return self.f


class VisitingStudent(Member):
    def __init__(self, i, n):
        super().__init__(i, n)

    def getScholarshipPercent(self):
        # visiting students are not in a degree program
        return 0

    def getTranscript(self):
        # not applicable to us, but we have to have this method
        return ""

    def payTuition(self, amt):
        # visiting students are billed by their home university
        pass


class FeeMgr:
    RATE = 4500.0
    LATE = 0.05

    def calc(self, s, sd, sm, sy, ed, em, ey, label, isLate, policy, discountLevel):
        # step 1: make sure the record is usable
        if s.getId() == "":
            print("bad id")
            return 0.0
        if s.getCredits() <= 0:
            print("bad credits")
            return 0.0
        if s.getProgram() == "":
            print("bad program")
            return 0.0

        total = 0.0
        base = s.getCredits() * FeeMgr.RATE

        if (s.getProgram() == "CSE" and s.getCredits() > 9
                and s.getWaiver() != "NONE"
                and not (em - sm > 4)
                and (s.getCredits() < 15 or s.getWaiver() == "MERIT")
                and s.getAtt().getLow() >= 60
                and not isLate):
            total = base * 0.8
        else:
            total = base

        # add up the individual course fees
        i = 0
        while i < len(s.getFees()):
            total = total + s.getFees()[i]
            i = i + 1

        low = s.getAtt().getLow()
        high = s.getAtt().getHigh()
        ok = policy.withinRange(low, high)
        if ok == False:
            total = total + 1000.0

        if discountLevel == 2:
            total = total - (base * 0.1)
        else:
            total = total - (base * 0.05)

        if isLate:
            total = total + total * FeeMgr.LATE

        print(label + " " + str(sd) + "/" + str(sm) + "/" + str(sy)
              + " - " + str(ed) + "/" + str(em) + "/" + str(ey))
        return total

    def proc(self, s):
        # step 1: make sure the record is usable
        if s.getId() == "":
            print("bad id")
            return 0.0
        if s.getCredits() <= 0:
            print("bad credits")
            return 0.0
        if s.getProgram() == "":
            print("bad program")
            return 0.0

        tmp = 0.0
        for x in s.getFees():
            tmp = tmp + x
        return tmp

    def sortFees(self, arr):
        n = len(arr)
        for a in range(n):
            for b in range(0, n - a - 1):
                if arr[b] > arr[b + 1]:
                    t = arr[b]
                    arr[b] = arr[b + 1]
                    arr[b + 1] = t
        return arr


class FeeReport:
    RATE = 4500.0
    LATE = 0.05

    def build(self, s):
        # step 1: make sure the record is usable
        if s.getId() == "":
            print("bad id")
            return ""
        if s.getCredits() <= 0:
            print("bad credits")
            return ""
        if s.getProgram() == "":
            print("bad program")
            return ""

        tmp = 0.0
        for x in s.getFees():
            tmp = tmp + x

        line = s.getName() + " | " + s.getProgram() + " | "
        line = line + str(s.getCredits()) + " cr | "
        line = line + str(s.getCredits() * FeeReport.RATE + tmp)
        return line

    def sortFees(self, arr):
        n = len(arr)
        for a in range(n):
            m = a
            for b in range(a + 1, n):
                if arr[b] < arr[m]:
                    m = b
            t = arr[a]
            arr[a] = arr[m]
            arr[m] = t
        return arr


def main():
    att = AttRange(75, 95)
    st = RegularStudent("24141001", "Rafi", 12, "CSE", "MERIT", att,
                        [1200.0, 800.0, 950.0])

    m = FeeMgr()
    r = FeeReport()
    p = AttPolicy()

    d = 1
    if st.getCredits() > 9:
        d = 2

    print(m.calc(st, 1, 1, 2026, 15, 5, 2026, "Spring 2026", False, p, d))
    print(m.proc(st))
    print(r.build(st))
    print(m.sortFees([950.0, 800.0, 1200.0]))
    print(r.sortFees([950.0, 800.0, 1200.0]))

    v = VisitingStudent("24141002", "Nadia")
    print(v.getScholarshipPercent())
    print(v.getTranscript())
    v.payTuition(5000.0)


main()

/*
 * CSE 470 - Software Engineering
 * Refactoring Practice Problem (Java)
 *
 * Semester Fee Processing System.
 *
 * The program works. Do not change what it prints.
 * Your job is to find the code smells and refactor them away.
 */

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

class AttRange {
    private int l;
    private int h;

    public AttRange(int l, int h) {
        this.l = l;
        this.h = h;
    }

    public int getLow() {
        return l;
    }

    public int getHigh() {
        return h;
    }
}

class AttPolicy {
    public boolean withinRange(int low, int high) {
        return low >= 60 && high <= 100;
    }
}

class Member {
    protected String i;
    protected String n;

    public Member(String i, String n) {
        this.i = i;
        this.n = n;
    }

    public String getId() {
        return i;
    }

    public String getName() {
        return n;
    }

    public int getScholarshipPercent() {
        return 25;
    }

    public String getTranscript() {
        return "TRANSCRIPT OF " + n;
    }

    public void payTuition(double amt) {
        System.out.println(n + " paid " + amt);
    }
}

class RegularStudent extends Member {
    private int cr;
    private String p;
    private String w;
    private AttRange a;
    private List<Double> f;

    public RegularStudent(String i, String n, int cr, String p, String w,
                          AttRange a, List<Double> f) {
        super(i, n);
        this.cr = cr;
        this.p = p;
        this.w = w;
        this.a = a;
        this.f = f;
    }

    public int getCredits() {
        return cr;
    }

    public String getProgram() {
        return p;
    }

    public String getWaiver() {
        return w;
    }

    public AttRange getAtt() {
        return a;
    }

    public List<Double> getFees() {
        return f;
    }
}

class VisitingStudent extends Member {
    public VisitingStudent(String i, String n) {
        super(i, n);
    }

    public int getScholarshipPercent() {
        // visiting students are not in a degree program
        return 0;
    }

    public String getTranscript() {
        // not applicable to us, but we have to have this method
        return "";
    }

    public void payTuition(double amt) {
        // visiting students are billed by their home university
    }
}

class FeeMgr {
    public static final double RATE = 4500.0;
    public static final double LATE = 0.05;

    public double calc(RegularStudent s, int sd, int sm, int sy, int ed, int em,
                       int ey, String label, boolean isLate, AttPolicy policy,
                       int discountLevel) {
        // step 1: make sure the record is usable
        if (s.getId().equals("")) {
            System.out.println("bad id");
            return 0.0;
        }
        if (s.getCredits() <= 0) {
            System.out.println("bad credits");
            return 0.0;
        }
        if (s.getProgram().equals("")) {
            System.out.println("bad program");
            return 0.0;
        }

        double total = 0.0;
        double base = s.getCredits() * FeeMgr.RATE;

        if (s.getProgram().equals("CSE") && s.getCredits() > 9
                && !s.getWaiver().equals("NONE")
                && !(em - sm > 4)
                && (s.getCredits() < 15 || s.getWaiver().equals("MERIT"))
                && s.getAtt().getLow() >= 60
                && !isLate) {
            total = base * 0.8;
        } else {
            total = base;
        }

        // add up the individual course fees
        int i = 0;
        while (i < s.getFees().size()) {
            total = total + s.getFees().get(i);
            i = i + 1;
        }

        int low = s.getAtt().getLow();
        int high = s.getAtt().getHigh();
        boolean ok = policy.withinRange(low, high);
        if (ok == false) {
            total = total + 1000.0;
        }

        if (discountLevel == 2) {
            total = total - (base * 0.1);
        } else {
            total = total - (base * 0.05);
        }

        if (isLate) {
            total = total + total * FeeMgr.LATE;
        }

        System.out.println(label + " " + sd + "/" + sm + "/" + sy
                + " - " + ed + "/" + em + "/" + ey);
        return total;
    }

    public double proc(RegularStudent s) {
        // step 1: make sure the record is usable
        if (s.getId().equals("")) {
            System.out.println("bad id");
            return 0.0;
        }
        if (s.getCredits() <= 0) {
            System.out.println("bad credits");
            return 0.0;
        }
        if (s.getProgram().equals("")) {
            System.out.println("bad program");
            return 0.0;
        }

        double tmp = 0.0;
        for (double x : s.getFees()) {
            tmp = tmp + x;
        }
        return tmp;
    }

    public double[] sortFees(double[] arr) {
        int n = arr.length;
        for (int a = 0; a < n; a++) {
            for (int b = 0; b < n - a - 1; b++) {
                if (arr[b] > arr[b + 1]) {
                    double t = arr[b];
                    arr[b] = arr[b + 1];
                    arr[b + 1] = t;
                }
            }
        }
        return arr;
    }
}

class FeeReport {
    public static final double RATE = 4500.0;
    public static final double LATE = 0.05;

    public String build(RegularStudent s) {
        // step 1: make sure the record is usable
        if (s.getId().equals("")) {
            System.out.println("bad id");
            return "";
        }
        if (s.getCredits() <= 0) {
            System.out.println("bad credits");
            return "";
        }
        if (s.getProgram().equals("")) {
            System.out.println("bad program");
            return "";
        }

        double tmp = 0.0;
        for (double x : s.getFees()) {
            tmp = tmp + x;
        }

        String line = s.getName() + " | " + s.getProgram() + " | ";
        line = line + s.getCredits() + " cr | ";
        line = line + (s.getCredits() * FeeReport.RATE + tmp);
        return line;
    }

    public double[] sortFees(double[] arr) {
        int n = arr.length;
        for (int a = 0; a < n; a++) {
            int m = a;
            for (int b = a + 1; b < n; b++) {
                if (arr[b] < arr[m]) {
                    m = b;
                }
            }
            double t = arr[a];
            arr[a] = arr[m];
            arr[m] = t;
        }
        return arr;
    }
}

public class FeeSystem {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        AttRange att = new AttRange(75, 95);
        List<Double> fees = new ArrayList<Double>();
        fees.add(1200.0);
        fees.add(800.0);
        fees.add(950.0);
        RegularStudent st = new RegularStudent("24141001", "Rafi", 12, "CSE",
                "MERIT", att, fees);

        FeeMgr m = new FeeMgr();
        FeeReport r = new FeeReport();
        AttPolicy p = new AttPolicy();

        int d = 1;
        if (st.getCredits() > 9) {
            d = 2;
        }

        System.out.println(m.calc(st, 1, 1, 2026, 15, 5, 2026, "Spring 2026",
                false, p, d));
        System.out.println(m.proc(st));
        System.out.println(r.build(st));
        System.out.println(java.util.Arrays.toString(
                m.sortFees(new double[]{950.0, 800.0, 1200.0})));
        System.out.println(java.util.Arrays.toString(
                r.sortFees(new double[]{950.0, 800.0, 1200.0})));

        VisitingStudent v = new VisitingStudent("24141002", "Nadia");
        System.out.println(v.getScholarshipPercent());
        System.out.println(v.getTranscript());
        v.payTuition(5000.0);
    }
}

Where the first number comes from

StepRunning total
Base fee — 12 credits × 4500.0054000.00
All seven waiver clauses are true → × 0.843200.00
Plus the course fees 1200 + 800 + 95046150.00
Attendance 75–95 sits inside 60–100 → no 1000.00 penalty46150.00

Line 2 and line 4 of the output are not the same fee

calc returns 40750.0 — the discounted semester fee. FeeReport.build prints 56950.0, which is 12 × 4500 + 2950 — the undiscounted base plus the course fees. They look like they should agree and they do not.

That is deliberate. When you unify the duplicated fee arithmetic in smell 6, it is tempting to make build reuse the semester-fee calculation. Do that and line 4 of the output changes. The reference solution keeps them separate: build uses baseFee() + totalCourseFees().

Compile each Java program into its own directory

FeeSystem.java and FeeSystemSolution.java both declare Member, RegularStudent, VisitingStudent and FeeReport in the default package. Compile them into the same directory and the second one's .class files silently overwrite the first one's — after which java FeeSystem dies with NoSuchMethodError, through no fault of your code.

javac -d out FeeSystem.java and javac -d out-solution FeeSystemSolution.java keep them apart. Python has no such problem: the two modules never share a namespace.

Smell 1 of 7Naming

1Inappropriate naming

Fowler's Mysterious Name — the cheapest smell to fix and the one that makes every other smell visible.

What the smell is

A name is the only documentation that cannot go stale, because the compiler carries it everywhere the thing goes. When a name is a single letter, an abbreviation, or a verb as vague as calc, the reader has to reconstruct the meaning from the body every single time — and reconstructing meaning is exactly the work refactoring is supposed to remove.

This smell comes first for a practical reason. Renaming is the safest refactoring there is: your editor can do it mechanically, and the risk of breaking behaviour is close to zero. Do it first and the remaining smells stop hiding. A method called proc looks harmless; the same method called totalCourseFees is obviously a duplicate of the loop in FeeReport.build.

Member.i, Member.none letter each, for an id and a namememberId, name
RegularStudent.cr, p, w, a, ffive one-letter fields on the class the whole program is aboutcredits, program, waiver, attendance, courseFees
AttRange, AttPolicy, getAtt()truncated words — three characters saved, one word lostAttendanceRange, AttendancePolicy, getAttendance()
FeeMgr“Mgr” is an abbreviation, and manager names a class that does everythingFeeCalculator
FeeMgr.calc(...)says it calculates, never says whatcalculateSemesterFee(...)
FeeMgr.proc(s)says nothing whatsoevertotalCourseFees(student)
RATE, LATErate of what? late what?FeeRates.PER_CREDIT, FeeRates.LATE_SURCHARGE
tmp, x, t, m, dmeaningless locals; t is a swap temp, d is a discount leveltotal, fee — most of them disappear entirely

ok, base, totalnot wrong, but base is a temp that a query can replacebaseFee() (see smell 3)

A name is not cosmetic

FeeMgr.proc and FeeReport.build contain the same three-line loop. Nobody notices while one of them is called proc. Rename it to totalCourseFees and the duplication in smell 6 announces itself.

Marking points

  • Every one-letter field and local is gone, except loop counters that are genuinely just counters.
  • No abbreviation survives: Mgr, Att, cr, sd/sm/sy.
  • Method names say what is produced, not that a computation happens: calculateSemesterFee, not calc or process.
  • Constants say what they measure — PER_CREDIT, not RATE.
  • The output is byte-identical. A rename that changes output is not a rename.
Smell 2 of 7Dispensables

2Comments

Fowler calls comments a deodorant: they are often used to mask a smell rather than remove it.

What the smell is

Comments are not bad. But when a comment explains what the next block of code does, it is usually standing in for a method name that was never written. The refactoring is mechanical: the comment becomes the method name, the block becomes the method body, and the comment disappears because it is now redundant.

The comments worth keeping are the ones that explain why — a policy decision, a business rule, a workaround for something outside the code. Those cannot be expressed as a method name, because they are not about the code at all.

This program has both kinds, and telling them apart is the exercise.

Where it is in this program

WhereThe commentWhat it is really saying
calc, proc, build — three copies# step 1: make sure the record is usable“the next ten lines are one operation” → Extract Method validate()
inside calc# add up the individual course feesa loop that needs a name → Extract Method sumCourseFees() (see smell 6)
VisitingStudent.getTranscript# not applicable to us, but we have to have this methodan apology for a broken hierarchy → fix the hierarchy (see smell 7)
the validation blocks(no comment at all)a precondition stated by a silent return 0.0 → Introduce Assertion
VisitingStudent.getScholarshipPercent# visiting students are not in a degree programKeep this one. It explains why the answer is 0, which no name can.
VisitingStudent.payTuition# visiting students are billed by their home universityKeep this one too. It is the billing policy, not a description of the code.

Your task

Go through every comment in the file and sort it into one of three piles: a name in disguise (extract a method and delete the comment), an apology (fix the design the comment is apologising for), or a genuine why (keep it, verbatim).

Then look for the opposite problem — a precondition that is enforced but never stated. calc returns 0.0 for a student with no id, and says nothing about it. That is a rule hiding inside a control-flow statement.

Where this one goes wrong

Do not simply delete the comments. Deleting # step 1: make sure the record is usable leaves the ten unexplained lines behind, which is worse than where you started. The comment goes away because the block it labelled became a method with that name.

Assertions are not on by default in Java

assert in Java is a no-op unless the JVM is started with -ea (java -ea FeeSystemSolution). Python evaluates assert unless you run python3 -O. Neither program's output changes here — the assertion passes — but the two languages disagree about whether it was even checked, which is worth knowing before you rely on one in production code.

Smell 3 of 7Bloaters

3Long method

FeeMgr.calc is 48 lines and does six unrelated jobs. Its refactored replacement is 10.

What the smell is

A method should do one thing at one level of detail. calc validates a record, picks a rate, sums a list, checks an attendance range, applies a discount, applies a late surcharge and prints a header — six jobs, none of them named, all sharing one mutable total.

The cost is not aesthetic. You cannot test the discount rule without also running the validation and the printing. You cannot reuse the fee summing, so it gets copied instead (smell 6). And you cannot read the seven-clause if without a pencil.

The heuristic Fowler gives is whenever you feel the need to comment something, write a method instead. This method comes pre-annotated with exactly those comments — they mark the extraction points for you.

Where it is in this program

The jobLines in calcExtract to
Validate the recordthe three if blocks under the “step 1” commentRegularStudent.hasValidRecord()
Decide the base feebase = s.getCredits() * FeeMgr.RATERegularStudent.baseFee() — Replace Temp with Query
Decide whether the waiver appliesthe seven-clause ifRegularStudent.qualifiesForWaiverDiscount(term, isLate) — Decompose Conditional
Sum the course feesthe index-driven while loopRegularStudent.totalCourseFees()
Penalise low attendancethe low / high / ok blockattendancePenalty(student, policy) — Preserve Whole Object
Apply the late surchargeif isLate: total = total + total * LATElateSurcharge(total, isLate)
Print the headerthe seven-piece string concatenationTerm.__str__ / Term.toString()

Your task

Extract each row of that table into a method whose name is the phrase in the first column. Extract one at a time and re-run after every extraction — that is what baby steps means, and it is the whole reason this exercise has a fixed expected output.

Two extractions deserve special attention. base is a temp: replace it with a query, so the base-fee formula lives in one place instead of being conceptually recomputed in three branches. And the seven-clause conditional should not just be moved — decompose it, so each clause gets a name that says what it tests.

Where this one goes wrong

Watch the order of operations. The late surcharge is applied to the total after the discount is subtracted, and the discount is computed from base, not from the running total. Extracting these in the wrong order changes the arithmetic — which is exactly the kind of mistake the fixed expected output is there to catch.

Decompose Conditionalthe seven-clause if → one named predicate built from six smaller named predicates
Preserve Whole Objectpolicy.withinRange(low, high) → policy.isAcceptable(attendance) (see smell 4)
Move Methodthe extracted predicates and sums land on RegularStudent, because that is where their data lives (see smell 5)

def calc(self, s, sd, sm, sy, ed, em, ey, label, isLate, policy, discountLevel):
    # step 1: make sure the record is usable
    if s.getId() == "":
        print("bad id")
        return 0.0
    if s.getCredits() <= 0:
        print("bad credits")
        return 0.0
    if s.getProgram() == "":
        print("bad program")
        return 0.0

    total = 0.0
    base = s.getCredits() * FeeMgr.RATE

    if (s.getProgram() == "CSE" and s.getCredits() > 9
            and s.getWaiver() != "NONE"
            and not (em - sm > 4)
            and (s.getCredits() < 15 or s.getWaiver() == "MERIT")
            and s.getAtt().getLow() >= 60
            and not isLate):
        total = base * 0.8
    else:
        total = base

    # add up the individual course fees
    i = 0
    while i < len(s.getFees()):
        total = total + s.getFees()[i]
        i = i + 1

    low = s.getAtt().getLow()
    high = s.getAtt().getHigh()
    ok = policy.withinRange(low, high)
    if ok == False:
        total = total + 1000.0

    if discountLevel == 2:
        total = total - (base * 0.1)
    else:
        total = total - (base * 0.05)

    if isLate:
        total = total + total * FeeMgr.LATE

    print(label + " " + str(sd) + "/" + str(sm) + "/" + str(sy)
          + " - " + str(ed) + "/" + str(em) + "/" + str(ey))
    return total

public double calc(RegularStudent s, int sd, int sm, int sy, int ed, int em,
                   int ey, String label, boolean isLate, AttPolicy policy,
                   int discountLevel) {
    // step 1: make sure the record is usable
    if (s.getId().equals("")) {
        System.out.println("bad id");
        return 0.0;
    }
    if (s.getCredits() <= 0) {
        System.out.println("bad credits");
        return 0.0;
    }
    if (s.getProgram().equals("")) {
        System.out.println("bad program");
        return 0.0;
    }

    double total = 0.0;
    double base = s.getCredits() * FeeMgr.RATE;

    if (s.getProgram().equals("CSE") && s.getCredits() > 9
            && !s.getWaiver().equals("NONE")
            && !(em - sm > 4)
            && (s.getCredits() < 15 || s.getWaiver().equals("MERIT"))
            && s.getAtt().getLow() >= 60
            && !isLate) {
        total = base * 0.8;
    } else {
        total = base;
    }

    // add up the individual course fees
    int i = 0;
    while (i < s.getFees().size()) {
        total = total + s.getFees().get(i);
        i = i + 1;
    }

    int low = s.getAtt().getLow();
    int high = s.getAtt().getHigh();
    boolean ok = policy.withinRange(low, high);
    if (ok == false) {
        total = total + 1000.0;
    }

    if (discountLevel == 2) {
        total = total - (base * 0.1);
    } else {
        total = total - (base * 0.05);
    }

    if (isLate) {
        total = total + total * FeeMgr.LATE;
    }

    System.out.println(label + " " + sd + "/" + sm + "/" + sy
            + " - " + ed + "/" + em + "/" + ey);
    return total;
}

def calculate_semester_fee(self, student, term, is_late, policy):
    if not student.has_valid_record():
        return 0.0

    total = self._fee_after_waiver(student, term, is_late)
    total += student.total_course_fees()
    total += self._attendance_penalty(student, policy)
    total -= student.base_fee() * student.discount_rate()
    total += self._late_surcharge(total, is_late)

    print(term)
    return total

def _fee_after_waiver(self, student, term, is_late):
    if student.qualifies_for_waiver_discount(term, is_late):
        return student.base_fee() * FeeRates.WAIVER_DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER
    return student.base_fee()

def _attendance_penalty(self, student, policy):
    # FIXES: Long Method - the original wrote

public double calculateSemesterFee(RegularStudent student, Term term,
                                   boolean isLate, AttendancePolicy policy) {
    if (!student.hasValidRecord()) {
        return 0.0;
    }

    double total = feeAfterWaiver(student, term, isLate);
    total += student.totalCourseFees();
    total += attendancePenalty(student, policy);
    total -= student.baseFee() * student.discountRate();
    total += lateSurcharge(total, isLate);

    System.out.println(term);
    return total;
}

private double feeAfterWaiver(RegularStudent student, Term term,
                              boolean isLate) {
    if (student.qualifiesForWaiverDiscount(term, isLate)) {
        return student.baseFee() * FeeRates.WAIVER_DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER;
    }
    return student.baseFee();
}

private double attendancePenalty(RegularStudent student,
                                 AttendancePolicy policy) {
    // FIXES: Long Method - the original wrote
    //       if (ok == false) { total = total + 1000.0; }
    //   with a magic number and a redundant `== false` comparison.
    if (policy.isAcceptable(student.getAttendance())) {
        return 0.0;
    }
    return FeeRates.LOW_ATTENDANCE_PENALTY;
}

private double lateSurcharge(double amount, boolean isLate) {
    if (isLate) {
        return amount * FeeRates.LATE_SURCHARGE;
    }
    return 0.0;
}

private boolean holdsAWaiver() {

not (em - sm > 4) was the worst clause of the seven

It is raw arithmetic on two of the eleven parameters, and it does not say what it means. Once the six date components become a Term (smell 4), it can be written as not term.spans_more_than(4) — a sentence. Naming a clause and introducing a parameter object are the same move seen from two directions.

Marking points

  • No method in the refactored program is longer than about a dozen lines.
  • base no longer exists as a temp; the base fee is a query.
  • The seven clauses each have a name; the composite predicate reads as a sentence.
  • The discount is still taken from the base fee, and the late surcharge is still applied last — the arithmetic order is unchanged.
  • The output is byte-identical.
Smell 4 of 7Bloaters

4Long parameter list

calc takes eleven parameters. Four of them do not need to be parameters at all.

What the smell is

A long parameter list is hard to call correctly and impossible to read at the call site. m.calc(st, 1, 1, 2026, 15, 5, 2026, "Spring 2026", False, p, d) — which 1 is the day and which is the month? Swap them and the program still compiles, still runs, and prints the wrong header.

Fowler's three cures apply in a fixed order of preference. If the values always travel together, they are an object nobody has written yet (Introduce Parameter Object). If a parameter is derived from another parameter, the callee can derive it itself (Replace Parameter with Method). If the caller unpacks an object just to pass its parts, pass the object (Preserve Whole Object).

All three apply here, and together they take the list from eleven to four.

Where it is in this program

ParametersWhy they should not be thereCure
sd, sm, sy, ed, em, eysix loose integers that always travel together and always mean the same two dates; label belongs with themIntroduce Parameter Object → SimpleDate, Term
discountLevelmain computes it from st.getCredits() — a student the method is already being handedReplace Parameter with Method → student.discountRate()
policy + the unpacked low / highthe caller pulls two ints out of AttRange and passes them separatelyPreserve Whole Object → policy.isAcceptable(attendance)
s, isLate, policygenuine inputs — they stay(keep)

Your task

Get calc down to four parameters or fewer. Target signature: calculateSemesterFee(student, term, isLate, policy).

Do the three cures separately, re-running after each. Introduce the parameter object first — it is the one that also cleans up the header printing and the em - sm > 4 clause, because a Term can answer spansMoreThan(4) itself.

Replace Parameter with MethoddiscountLevel → student.discountRate(), and the three-line computation in main disappears
Preserve Whole ObjectwithinRange(low, high) → isAcceptable(attendance)

Smell 5 of 7Couplers

5Feature envy

RegularStudent is a bag of getters. Every calculation about a student happens somewhere else.

What the smell is

Feature Envy is a method that is more interested in another class than in the one it lives in. The test is mechanical: count the calls. If a method touches another object's data more often than its own, it wants to live on that object.

FeeMgr.calc calls getCredits(), getProgram(), getWaiver(), getFees() and getAtt() — nine times in one method — and touches nothing of its own except two constants. FeeReport.build does the same with four. RegularStudent itself has no behaviour at all; it is Fowler's Data Class, the other half of the same problem.

The same pattern repeats one level down: AttPolicy.withinRange pulls getLow() and getHigh() out of AttRange and does the comparison itself, instead of asking the range whether it is within bounds.

Where it is in this program

MethodData it reaches forWhere it belongs
FeeMgr.calcgetCredits(), getProgram(), getWaiver(), getAtt(), getFees() — nine callsthe fee arithmetic moves onto RegularStudent
FeeMgr.procgetFees(), plus the whole validation trioRegularStudent.totalCourseFees()
FeeReport.buildgetName(), getProgram(), getCredits(), getFees() — and multiplies credits by a rate it keeps its own copy ofRegularStudent.baseFee() and totalCourseFees(); the report keeps only the formatting
AttPolicy.withinRangeAttRange.getLow(), AttRange.getHigh()AttendanceRange.isWithin(min, max)

Your task

Move every calculation to the class that owns the data it works on. When you are done, FeeReport.build should contain string formatting and nothing else, and FeeCalculator should orchestrate — call things in order — without doing arithmetic on somebody else's fields.

Keep the getters. Moving behaviour onto RegularStudent does not mean deleting its accessors; it means the accessors stop being the only thing it offers.

Where this one goes wrong

Feature Envy is not a licence to move everything. FeeCalculator legitimately owns the sequence — validate, then waiver, then fees, then penalty, then discount, then surcharge — and the printing. A calculator that has been dissolved entirely into the student is a different design mistake, not a fix.

Data Class is the same smell from the other side

A class with nothing but getters and a class that does another object's arithmetic are two symptoms of one missing decision: nobody said where the behaviour lives. Fixing Feature Envy on FeeMgr and fixing Data Class on RegularStudent are the same edit.

Marking points

  • RegularStudent has methods that answer questions, not only methods that hand out fields.
  • FeeReport.build contains formatting and a validation guard — no arithmetic.
  • FeeCalculator still owns the order of the steps. It has not been dissolved.
  • AttendanceRange decides whether it is in range; the policy supplies the bounds.
  • No class holds a private copy of another class's constant to do its arithmetic with.
Smell 6 of 7Dispensables

6Duplicated code

All five levels of duplication are in this one program — and only one of them is visible to a copy-paste detector.

What the smell is

Duplication is the smell every tool claims to find and every tool finds only the easiest kind. It comes in levels, and they get harder to see as you go down:

Literal — the same characters twice. Semantic — the same intent written two different ways, so no diff tool matches them. Data — the same constant declared in two places, ready to drift apart the moment one is updated. Conceptual — two different algorithms solving one problem. Logical steps — the same sequence of operations repeated, even though the individual lines differ.

This program has one instance of each. Find all five.

Where it is in this program

LevelWhereRemedy
Literaltmp = 0.0 + for x in s.getFees() is byte-identical in FeeMgr.proc and FeeReport.buildExtract Method, then Move Method onto the student
SemanticFeeMgr.calc sums the same list with an index-driven while loop — same intent, different shape, so no tool matches itSubstitute Algorithm, then Extract Method
DataRATE = 4500.0 and LATE = 0.05 are declared in both FeeMgr and FeeReportPull Up Field into one constants holder
ConceptualFeeMgr.sortFees is a bubble sort; FeeReport.sortFees is a selection sort. Two algorithms, one job, not a line in commonSubstitute Algorithm — keep one, or delegate to the library sort
Logical stepsthe same three-step check — id, credits, program — appears in calc, proc and buildExtract Method → hasValidRecord(); the differing return values are the hook for Form Template Method

The differing return values are the interesting part

The three validation copies are not quite identical: calc and proc return 0.0, build returns "". That difference is why a naive “extract the common block” fails, and it is exactly the situation Form Template Method exists for — the shared steps move up, the differing result stays with the caller. The reference solution takes the simpler route available here: the extracted method returns a boolean and each caller supplies its own failure value.

Your task

Find one instance of each of the five levels and remove it. Work from the easiest to the hardest — the literal one first, the logical-steps one last.

For the conceptual duplication, decide deliberately: do you keep the bubble sort, keep the selection sort, or delegate to the language's sort? Whichever you choose, there must be exactly one sorting routine in the program when you are finished, and it must produce the same list.

Where this one goes wrong

Removing duplication is the one refactoring most likely to change behaviour by accident, because the copies are never quite identical. Diff them character by character before you merge them — the 0.0 versus "" return values, and FeeReport's use of FeeReport.RATE rather than FeeMgr.RATE, are exactly the kind of difference that hides in “identical” code.

Move Methodboth of them belong on RegularStudent, not on the callers
Substitute Algorithmone sort survives; the while loop becomes the same summation as everyone else's
Pull Up FieldRATE and LATE → a single FeeRates holder
Form Template Methodif you keep the shared validation returning different types per caller

        m = a
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            if arr[b] < arr[m]:
                m = b
        t = arr[a]
        arr[a] = arr[m]
        arr[m] = t
    return arr

public double[] sortFees(double[] arr) {
    int n = arr.length;
    for (int a = 0; a < n; a++) {
        for (int b = 0; b < n - a - 1; b++) {
            if (arr[b] > arr[b + 1]) {
                double t = arr[b];
                arr[b] = arr[b + 1];
                arr[b + 1] = t;
            }
        }
    }
    return arr;
}

The one place the reference solution changes more than the output shows

The original sortFees sorts the caller's list in place and returns it. The replacement returns a new sorted list and leaves the argument untouched — sorted(fees) in Python, Arrays.copyOf then Arrays.sort in Java.

No caller in this program depends on the mutation, so the printed output is identical. But “the output did not change” is not the same as “nothing changed”. If you make this substitution, say so — and in a real codebase, check every caller first.

Marking points

  • The fee list is summed in exactly one place.
  • 4500.0 and 0.05 each appear exactly once in the whole program.
  • There is exactly one sorting routine, and both call sites use it.
  • The validation sequence exists once, and each caller still returns its own failure value (0.0 or "").
  • Every magic number that survived — 1000.0, 0.8, 0.1, 9, 60, 100 — has a name.
Smell 7 of 7OO abusers

7Refused bequest

VisitingStudent inherits three methods and refuses all three. The hierarchy is asserting something that is not true.

What the smell is

Inheritance is a promise: every subclass is a superclass, and can honour everything the superclass declares. When a subclass overrides inherited methods to return nothing, return zero, or do nothing at all, it is refusing the bequest — and the promise was false.

Member declares getScholarshipPercent(), getTranscript() and payTuition(amt). A visiting student has no scholarship, no transcript from this university, and pays no tuition here. All three overrides exist purely to cancel what was inherited, and one of them is even accompanied by a comment apologising for its own existence.

The empty payTuition is the strongest signal. A method whose body is empty is a class saying this operation does not apply to me in the only vocabulary the hierarchy allows.

Where it is in this program

Inherited memberWhat VisitingStudent does with itVerdict
getScholarshipPercent()overrides it to return 0the concept does not apply — a non-degree member has no scholarship rate, not a rate of zero
getTranscript()overrides it to return "", with the comment “not applicable to us, but we have to have this method”the comment is the diagnosis — the code admits the design is wrong
payTuition(amt)overrides it with an empty bodythe strongest form of refusal there is
getId(), getName()uses both, unchangedthese are the only things Member should ever have declared

Your task

Push everything that only degree students need down into RegularStudent, leaving Member with identity and nothing else. When you are done, VisitingStudent should override nothing — because there is nothing left to refuse.

Then decide what happens to the three call sites in main. Two of them print, so their output must be preserved; the third calls the empty payTuition and prints nothing at all.

Where this one goes wrong

v.payTuition(5000.0) produces no output — the override's body is empty. That means deleting the call entirely preserves the program's output exactly. Convince yourself of that before you delete it, and be able to say why deleting a call is a safe refactoring here and would not be if the body printed anything.

VisitingStudent in Java still needs a constructor

Python's VisitingStudent becomes a class body containing nothing but a comment and pass — it inherits Member.__init__ for free. Java has no constructor inheritance, so the subclass keeps a two-line constructor that only calls super. That is a language difference, not a surviving smell.

The reference solution is one answer, not the only one

NonDegreeMemberPolicy puts the non-degree rules somewhere explicit, outside the hierarchy — but note that its two methods ignore the member they are handed, which is a seam left for rules that later do depend on the member.

The alternative in the marking key is cleaner in a larger system: declare a Billable interface with payTuition and getTranscript, let RegularStudent implement it, and let VisitingStudent simply not. Then the type system, rather than an empty method body, is what says this does not apply. Either answer earns full marks if the reasoning is stated.

Marking points

  • Member declares identity and nothing else.
  • VisitingStudent overrides nothing — in Java, beyond the constructor it cannot inherit.
  • No method body in the program is empty, and no method returns a “not applicable” placeholder to satisfy a superclass.
  • The two “why” comments about visiting students still exist somewhere.
  • Lines 7 and 8 of the output — 0 and the blank line — are still produced.

All seven smells removed, in both languages, printing exactly what the original printed.

"""
CSE 470 - Software Engineering
Refactoring Practice Problem - SOLUTION (Python)

Semester Fee Processing System, refactored.

External behaviour is unchanged: this file prints exactly what the
original smelly version printed. Every comment below names the smell
that was present in the original code and the Fowler refactoring used
to remove it.
"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Duplicated Code (data level)
#   Original: RATE = 4500.0 and LATE = 0.05 were declared TWICE - once in
#   FeeMgr and once in FeeReport. Two copies of the same constant drift
#   apart the moment one of them is updated.
#   Refactoring: Pull Up Field - one authoritative home for the rates.
#
# FIXES: Inappropriate Naming
#   Original: RATE and LATE said nothing about what they measure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class FeeRates:
    PER_CREDIT = 4500.0
    LATE_SURCHARGE = 0.05
    LOW_ATTENDANCE_PENALTY = 1000.0
    WAIVER_DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER = 0.8
    HIGH_DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.1
    STANDARD_DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.05
    HIGH_DISCOUNT_CREDIT_THRESHOLD = 9


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Refused Bequest (Push Down Method)
#   Original: VisitingStudent carried three do-nothing overrides because
#   Member forced degree-student behaviour on every subclass. The rules
#   for a non-degree member are stated once, here, outside the hierarchy,
#   so no class has to fake an implementation it does not want.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class NonDegreeMemberPolicy:
    def scholarship_percent(self, member):
        return 0

    def transcript(self, member):
        return ""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Inappropriate Naming
#   Original: class AttRange with fields l and h.
#   Refactoring: Rename Class / Rename Variable.
#
# FIXES: Feature Envy
#   Original: AttPolicy pulled getLow() and getHigh() out of AttRange and
#   did the comparison itself. Data and the behaviour that acts on it
#   belong together, so the comparison now lives here.
#   Refactoring: Move Method.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class AttendanceRange:
    def __init__(self, low, high):
        # FIXES: Comments (Introduce Assertion)
        #   Original: preconditions on the data were never stated at all -
        #   a nonsensical range would have silently produced a wrong fee.
        assert low <= high, "attendance low must not exceed high"
        self.low = low
        self.high = high

    def get_low(self):
        return self.low

    def get_high(self):
        return self.high

    def is_within(self, minimum_low, maximum_high):
        return self.low >= minimum_low and self.high <= maximum_high


class AttendancePolicy:
    MINIMUM_ATTENDANCE = 60
    MAXIMUM_ATTENDANCE = 100

    # FIXES: Long Parameter List / Long Method (Preserve Whole Object)
    #   Original: withinRange(low, high) forced every caller to write
    #       low  = s.getAtt().getLow()
    #       high = s.getAtt().getHigh()
    #       ok   = policy.withinRange(low, high)
    #   Refactoring: pass the whole object; the two unpacking lines vanish.
    def is_acceptable(self, attendance):
        return attendance.is_within(self.MINIMUM_ATTENDANCE,
                                    self.MAXIMUM_ATTENDANCE)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Long Parameter List (Introduce Parameter Object)
#   Original: calc() took sd, sm, sy, ed, em, ey - six loose integers that
#   always travelled together and always meant the same two dates.
#   Refactoring: Introduce Parameter Object - SimpleDate and Term.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class SimpleDate:
    def __init__(self, day, month, year):
        self.day = day
        self.month = month
        self.year = year

    def get_month(self):
        return self.month

    def __str__(self):
        return str(self.day) + "/" + str(self.month) + "/" + str(self.year)


class Term:
    def __init__(self, label, start, end):
        self.label = label
        self.start = start
        self.end = end

    # FIXES: Long Method (Extract Method)
    #   Original: the condition read `not (em - sm > 4)`, a raw arithmetic
    #   expression buried inside an already unreadable if-statement.
    def spans_more_than(self, months):
        return self.end.get_month() - self.start.get_month() > months

    def __str__(self):
        return self.label + " " + str(self.start) + " - " + str(self.end)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Refused Bequest (Push Down Method)
#   Original: Member declared getScholarshipPercent(), getTranscript() and
#   payTuition(). VisitingStudent inherited all three and then refused the
#   bequest - returning 0, returning "", and leaving payTuition empty.
#   Refactoring: Push Down Method. Member now holds identity only, so
#   there is nothing left for a subclass to neuter.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class Member:
    def __init__(self, member_id, name):
        self.member_id = member_id
        self.name = name

    def get_id(self):
        return self.member_id

    def get_name(self):
        return self.name


class RegularStudent(Member):
    # FIXES: Inappropriate Naming
    #   Original: fields cr, p, w, a, f and accessor getAtt().
    #   Refactoring: Rename Variable / Rename Method.
    def __init__(self, member_id, name, credits, program, waiver,
                 attendance, course_fees):
        super().__init__(member_id, name)
        self.credits = credits
        self.program = program
        self.waiver = waiver
        self.attendance = attendance
        self.course_fees = course_fees

    def get_credits(self):
        return self.credits

    def get_program(self):
        return self.program

    def get_waiver(self):
        return self.waiver

    def get_attendance(self):
        return self.attendance

    def get_course_fees(self):
        return self.course_fees

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # FIXES: Feature Envy (Move Method)
    #   Original: RegularStudent was a bag of getters. FeeMgr and FeeReport
    #   reached into it over and over - getCredits(), getProgram(),
    #   getWaiver(), getFees(), getAtt() - and did all the arithmetic
    #   themselves. The behaviour below is now where its data lives.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # FIXES: Duplicated Code (literal AND semantic levels)
    #   Original literal duplication: the loop
    #       for x in s.getFees(): tmp = tmp + x
    #   was copied verbatim into FeeMgr.proc and FeeReport.build.
    #   Original semantic duplication: FeeMgr.calc summed the very same
    #   list with an index-driven while loop - same intent, different
    #   shape, so it did not even look like a duplicate.
    #   Refactoring: Extract Method + Substitute Algorithm. One summation.
    def total_course_fees(self):
        return sum(self.course_fees)

    # FIXES: Long Method (Replace Temp with Query)
    #   Original: `base = s.getCredits() * FeeMgr.RATE` was a temp that the
    #   rest of calc() leaned on. If the base-fee formula changes, it must
    #   now change in exactly one place.
    def base_fee(self):
        return self.credits * FeeRates.PER_CREDIT

    # FIXES: Long Method (Decompose Conditional) / conditional complexity
    #   Original: a seven-clause boolean mixing and, or and two negations
    #   sat inline in calc(). Nobody could read it aloud, let alone test it.
    #       if (s.getProgram() == "CSE" and s.getCredits() > 9
    #               and s.getWaiver() != "NONE"
    #               and not (em - sm > 4)
    #               and (s.getCredits() < 15 or s.getWaiver() == "MERIT")
    #               and s.getAtt().getLow() >= 60
    #               and not isLate):
    #   Refactoring: Decompose Conditional - extract the condition into a
    #   named predicate, then extract its parts into named predicates too.
    def qualifies_for_waiver_discount(self, term, is_late):
        return (self._is_in_discounted_program()
                and self._carries_enough_credits()
                and self._holds_a_waiver()
                and not term.spans_more_than(4)
                and self._waiver_still_applies()
                and self._meets_minimum_attendance()
                and not is_late)

    def _is_in_discounted_program(self):
        return self.program == "CSE"

    def _carries_enough_credits(self):
        return self.credits > 9

    def _holds_a_waiver(self):
        return self.waiver != "NONE"

    def _waiver_still_applies(self):
        return self.credits < 15 or self.waiver == "MERIT"

    def _meets_minimum_attendance(self):
        return self.attendance.get_low() >= AttendancePolicy.MINIMUM_ATTENDANCE

    # FIXES: Long Parameter List (Replace Parameter with Method)
    #   Original: calc() accepted discountLevel as its eleventh parameter,
    #   and main() computed it from the student it was already passing in:
    #       d = 1
    #       if st.getCredits() > 9: d = 2
    #   The callee can ask the student itself, so the parameter is dropped.
    def discount_rate(self):
        if self.credits > FeeRates.HIGH_DISCOUNT_CREDIT_THRESHOLD:
            return FeeRates.HIGH_DISCOUNT_RATE
        return FeeRates.STANDARD_DISCOUNT_RATE

    # FIXES: Duplicated Code (logical-steps level)
    #   Original: the identical three-step check - empty id, non-positive
    #   credits, empty program - was written out in FeeMgr.calc,
    #   FeeMgr.proc and FeeReport.build. Three copies of one rule.
    # FIXES: Comments
    #   Original: each copy was introduced by the comment
    #       # step 1: make sure the record is usable
    #   A comment labelling a block is a request to extract that block into
    #   a method whose name says what the comment said.
    #   Refactoring: Extract Method + Move Method (the rule is about the
    #   student's own data, so it belongs on the student).
    def has_valid_record(self):
        if self.member_id == "":
            print("bad id")
            return False
        if self.credits <= 0:
            print("bad credits")
            return False
        if self.program == "":
            print("bad program")
            return False
        return True

    def get_scholarship_percent(self):
        return 25

    def get_transcript(self):
        return "TRANSCRIPT OF " + self.name

    def pay_tuition(self, amount):
        print(self.name + " paid " + str(amount))


class VisitingStudent(Member):
    # FIXES: Refused Bequest (Push Down Method)
    #   Original: this class existed almost entirely to cancel what it
    #   inherited - three overrides that returned 0, returned "" and did
    #   nothing, each apologised for by a comment. Now that Member carries
    #   no degree-student behaviour, VisitingStudent refuses nothing and
    #   needs no overrides at all.
    pass


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Duplicated Code (conceptual level)
#   Original: FeeMgr.sortFees was a bubble sort and FeeReport.sortFees was
#   a selection sort. Two different algorithms solving one problem is
#   duplication even though not a single line matches.
#   Refactoring: Substitute Algorithm - keep one implementation.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def sorted_fees(fees):
    return sorted(fees)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXES: Inappropriate Naming
#   Original: class FeeMgr, methods calc() and proc(). "Mgr" is an
#   abbreviation, "calc" does not say what it calculates, and "proc" says
#   nothing whatsoever.
#   Refactoring: Rename Class / Rename Method.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class FeeCalculator:

    # FIXES: Long Method (Extract Method, Replace Temp with Query,
    #        Decompose Conditional, Preserve Whole Object)
    # FIXES: Long Parameter List (11 parameters -> 4)
    #   Original signature:
    #       calc(self, s, sd, sm, sy, ed, em, ey, label, isLate, policy,
    #            discountLevel)
    #   Original body: ~50 lines doing six unrelated jobs - validating,
    #   choosing a rate, summing fees, checking attendance, discounting,
    #   applying a late surcharge and printing a header.
    def calculate_semester_fee(self, student, term, is_late, policy):
        if not student.has_valid_record():
            return 0.0

        total = self._fee_after_waiver(student, term, is_late)
        total += student.total_course_fees()
        total += self._attendance_penalty(student, policy)
        total -= student.base_fee() * student.discount_rate()
        total += self._late_surcharge(total, is_late)

        print(term)
        return total

    def _fee_after_waiver(self, student, term, is_late):
        if student.qualifies_for_waiver_discount(term, is_late):
            return student.base_fee() * FeeRates.WAIVER_DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER
        return student.base_fee()

    def _attendance_penalty(self, student, policy):
        # FIXES: Long Method - the original wrote
        #       if ok == False: total = total + 1000.0
        #   with a magic number and a redundant `== False` comparison.
        if policy.is_acceptable(student.get_attendance()):
            return 0.0
        return FeeRates.LOW_ATTENDANCE_PENALTY

    def _late_surcharge(self, amount, is_late):
        if is_late:
            return amount * FeeRates.LATE_SURCHARGE
        return 0.0

    # FIXES: Duplicated Code (literal + semantic) and Feature Envy
    #   Original: proc() re-validated the record and re-summed the fee list
    #   with its own copy of the loop. Both jobs now belong to the student.
    def total_course_fees(self, student):
        if not student.has_valid_record():
            return 0.0
        return student.total_course_fees()


class FeeReport:

    # FIXES: Duplicated Code (literal, data and logical-steps levels)
    #   Original: build() carried its own copy of the validation sequence,
    #   its own copy of the summing loop, and its own copy of the RATE
    #   constant. All three are now shared.
    # FIXES: Feature Envy
    #   Original: this method computed s.getCredits() * RATE + tmp, doing
    #   the student's arithmetic on the student's data.
    def build(self, student):
        if not student.has_valid_record():
            return ""

        total = student.base_fee() + student.total_course_fees()
        return (student.get_name() + " | " + student.get_program() + " | "
                + str(student.get_credits()) + " cr | " + str(total))


def main():
    attendance = AttendanceRange(75, 95)
    student = RegularStudent("24141001", "Rafi", 12, "CSE", "MERIT",
                             attendance, [1200.0, 800.0, 950.0])

    calculator = FeeCalculator()
    report = FeeReport()
    policy = AttendancePolicy()

    # FIXES: Long Parameter List (Introduce Parameter Object)
    #   Original call site passed six loose date components plus a label.
    spring = Term("Spring 2026", SimpleDate(1, 1, 2026), SimpleDate(15, 5, 2026))

    # FIXES: Long Parameter List (Replace Parameter with Method)
    #   Original: main computed the discount level here and passed it in.
    #   That block is gone - the student answers the question itself.
    print(calculator.calculate_semester_fee(student, spring, False, policy))
    print(calculator.total_course_fees(student))
    print(report.build(student))

    # FIXES: Duplicated Code (conceptual level)
    #   Original: two calls to two different sorting algorithms.
    print(sorted_fees([950.0, 800.0, 1200.0]))
    print(sorted_fees([950.0, 800.0, 1200.0]))

    # FIXES: Refused Bequest (Push Down Method)
    #   Original:
    #       v = VisitingStudent("24141002", "Nadia")
    #       print(v.getScholarshipPercent())   # overridden to return 0
    #       print(v.getTranscript())           # overridden to return ""
    #       v.payTuition(5000.0)               # overridden to do nothing
    #   Scholarships, transcripts and tuition now live on RegularStudent
    #   only. The empty payTuition call disappears entirely - a call that
    #   did nothing is not worth keeping - and the two "not applicable"
    #   answers come from an explicit policy object instead of being
    #   hidden inside do-nothing overrides.
    visiting = VisitingStudent("24141002", "Nadia")
    non_degree = NonDegreeMemberPolicy()
    print(non_degree.scholarship_percent(visiting))
    print(non_degree.transcript(visiting))


main()
