import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

// ---------- Observer interface ----------
interface Observer {
    void update(Subject subject);
}

// ---------- Subject ----------
class Subject {
    private final List<Observer> observers = new ArrayList<>();

    public void attach(Observer observer) {
        observers.add(observer);
    }

    public void detach(Observer observer) {
        observers.remove(observer);
    }

    public void notifyObservers() {                 // notify() is final on Object
        for (Observer observer : new ArrayList<>(observers)) {
            observer.update(this);
        }
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Subject ----------
class Auction extends Subject {
    private final String item;
    private int highestBid = 0;
    private String highestBidder = "nobody";

    public Auction(String item) {
        this.item = item;
    }

    public void placeBid(String name, int amount) {
        if (amount > highestBid) {
            highestBid = amount;
            highestBidder = name;
            notifyObservers();
        }
    }

    public String getItem() {
        return item;
    }

    public int getHighestBid() {
        return highestBid;
    }

    public String getHighestBidder() {
        return highestBidder;
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Observers ----------
class Bidder implements Observer {
    private final String name;

    public Bidder(String name) {
        this.name = name;
    }

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        Auction auction = (Auction) subject;
        String item = auction.getItem();
        int amount = auction.getHighestBid();
        String leader = auction.getHighestBidder();
        String tag = leader.equals(name) ? "you lead" : leader + " leads";
        System.out.println("[" + name + "] " + item
                + " now BDT " + amount + " - " + tag);
    }

    public void join(Auction auction) {
        auction.attach(this);
        System.out.println(name + " joined the auction");
    }

    public void leave(Auction auction) {
        auction.detach(this);
        System.out.println(name + " left the auction");
    }
}

class BidLogger implements Observer {
    private final List<String> entries = new ArrayList<>();

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        Auction auction = (Auction) subject;
        int amount = auction.getHighestBid();
        String leader = auction.getHighestBidder();
        entries.add(amount + " by " + leader);
        int count = entries.size();
        System.out.println("[Logger] bid #" + count + " recorded");
    }
}

public class AuctionDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Auction auction = new Auction("Antique Clock");

        Bidder nabil = new Bidder("Nabil");
        Bidder sadia = new Bidder("Sadia");
        BidLogger logger = new BidLogger();

        nabil.join(auction);
        sadia.join(auction);
        auction.attach(logger);

        auction.placeBid("Nabil", 5000);
        sadia.leave(auction);
        auction.placeBid("Sadia", 7500);
    }
}

RoleClass
ObserverObserver
SubjectSubject
Concrete SubjectAuction
Concrete ObserversBidder, BidLogger

Marking points

  • notify() is called from inside place_bid, not from the driver, and only when the bid actually beats the current price.
  • Auction never names Bidder anywhere. If it does, the one-to-many decoupling is not there.
  • The observer reads state back through the subject it was handed (subject.get_highest_bid()) rather than having the price pushed in as an argument — either is defensible, but ask them which one keeps the update signature stable when the subject grows more state.
  • detach actually removes: Sadia produces no output on the second bid even though she placed it.
  • BidLogger proves observers need not be homogeneous.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • Both languages expose one getter per piece of state — getHighestBid() and getHighestBidder() — so the two listings line up method for method. Python could have returned a single tuple and Java a small Price record; pushing the values in as update arguments is the third option. Comparing the three is the pull-vs-push decision the marking notes mention.
  • leader.equals(name), never leader == name. == on strings compares references, and it would appear to work here because of the string pool, then fail the moment a name is read from input. This is the single most common Java bug in first-year code.
Practice — Set BSingleton

One Print Spooler for the Lab

Exactly one, created late

The story

The computer lab has one printer. Every machine in the lab currently builds its own spooler object before sending a file, so each PC ends up with a private queue: the admin console shows an empty queue even while three jobs are waiting, and the log shows the printer port being locked once per machine.

The lab wants exactly one spooler object for the entire lab, reachable from any machine, and it must not be created when the lab software boots — the port should only be locked the first time somebody actually prints.

        self.queue = []

    def add_job(self, pc, filename):
        self.queue.append((pc, filename))
        print(f"queued '{filename}' from {pc} (position {len(self.queue)})")

        spooler = PrintSpooler()
        print(f"jobs waiting: {len(spooler.pending())}")

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

class Job {
    final String pc;
    final String filename;

    Job(String pc, String filename) {
        this.pc = pc;
        this.filename = filename;
    }
}

class PrintSpooler {
    List<Job> queue;

    PrintSpooler() {
        System.out.println("Starting print spooler and locking the printer port...");
        this.queue = new ArrayList<>();
    }

    void addJob(String pc, String filename) {
        queue.add(new Job(pc, filename));
        System.out.println("queued '" + filename + "' from " + pc
                + " (position " + queue.size() + ")");
    }

    List<Job> pending() {
        return queue;
    }
}

class LabComputer {
    final String pcId;

    LabComputer(String pcId) {
        this.pcId = pcId;
    }

    void printFile(String filename) {
        PrintSpooler spooler = new PrintSpooler();
        spooler.addJob(pcId, filename);
    }
}

class AdminConsole {
    void status() {
        PrintSpooler spooler = new PrintSpooler();
        System.out.println("jobs waiting: " + spooler.pending().size());
        for (Job job : spooler.pending()) {
            System.out.println("  - " + job.filename + " (" + job.pc + ")");
        }
    }
}

# ---------- Singleton ----------
class PrintSpooler:
    _instance = None

    def __new__(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:                      # lazy creation
            print("Starting print spooler and locking the printer port...")
            cls._instance = super(PrintSpooler, cls).__new__(cls)
            cls._instance.queue = []                   # initialise ONCE, here
        return cls._instance

    def add_job(self, pc, filename):
        self.queue.append((pc, filename))
        position = len(self.queue)
        print(f"queued '{filename}' from {pc} (position {position})")

    def pending(self):
        return self.queue


# ---------- Clients: each one asks for the spooler independently ----------
class LabComputer:
    def __init__(self, pc_id):
        self.pc_id = pc_id

    def print_file(self, filename):
        spooler = PrintSpooler()
        spooler.add_job(self.pc_id, filename)


class AdminConsole:
    def status(self):
        spooler = PrintSpooler()
        waiting = len(spooler.pending())
        print(f"jobs waiting: {waiting}")
        for pc, filename in spooler.pending():
            print(f"  - {filename} ({pc})")

    print("--- lab opened, printer not touched yet ---")

    LabComputer("PC-07").print_file("thesis.pdf")
    LabComputer("PC-12").print_file("lab_report.docx")

    AdminConsole().status()
    print("same object?", PrintSpooler() is PrintSpooler())

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

// ---------- One queued job (Python used a plain tuple) ----------
class Job {
    final String pc;
    final String filename;

    Job(String pc, String filename) {
        this.pc = pc;
        this.filename = filename;
    }
}

// ---------- Singleton ----------
class PrintSpooler {
    private static PrintSpooler instance;                  // the one instance
    private final List<Job> queue = new ArrayList<>();

    private PrintSpooler() {                               // nobody else can build one
        System.out.println("Starting print spooler and locking the printer port...");
    }

    public static PrintSpooler getInstance() {             // lazy creation
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new PrintSpooler();
        }
        return instance;
    }

    public void addJob(String pc, String filename) {
        queue.add(new Job(pc, filename));
        int position = queue.size();
        System.out.println("queued '" + filename + "' from " + pc
                + " (position " + position + ")");
    }

    public List<Job> pending() {
        return queue;
    }
}

// ---------- Clients: each one asks for the spooler independently ----------
class LabComputer {
    private final String pcId;

    public LabComputer(String pcId) {
        this.pcId = pcId;
    }

    public void printFile(String filename) {
        PrintSpooler.getInstance().addJob(pcId, filename);
    }
}

class AdminConsole {
    public void status() {
        PrintSpooler spooler = PrintSpooler.getInstance();
        int waiting = spooler.pending().size();
        System.out.println("jobs waiting: " + waiting);
        for (Job job : spooler.pending()) {
            System.out.println("  - " + job.filename + " (" + job.pc + ")");
        }
    }
}

public class PrintSpoolerDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("--- lab opened, printer not touched yet ---");

        new LabComputer("PC-07").printFile("thesis.pdf");
        new LabComputer("PC-12").printFile("lab_report.docx");

        new AdminConsole().status();
        System.out.println("same object? "
                + (PrintSpooler.getInstance() == PrintSpooler.getInstance()));
    }
}

RoleClass

ClientsLabComputer, AdminConsole

Marking points

  • __new__ is overridden, _instance is a class attribute, and the guard is if cls._instance is None — this is what makes it lazy.
  • The start-up message prints once and only after the first client prints. Creating the instance at import time is not lazy.
  • queue is initialised inside the __new__ guard (or with an _initialised flag in __init__). A plain __init__ that assigns self.queue = [] empties the queue on every later call, so the admin console reports 0 jobs. This is the trap in this problem.
  • LabComputer and AdminConsole are untouched.
  • Common alternatives worth accepting: a get_instance() classmethod, a decorator, or a module-level instance — but the clients here call PrintSpooler() directly, so a get_instance() solution has to edit them, which the brief forbids. Worth making them notice that.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • The brief's “do not touch the clients” rule cannot be honoured in Java: with a private constructor, new PrintSpooler() stops compiling, so both clients must move to PrintSpooler.getInstance(). Compare with a2 — the same limitation, and it is the reason getInstance() is the textbook Java form while Python textbooks show __new__.
  • pending() returns the live internal list, so any caller can mutate the queue. Collections.unmodifiableList(queue) (or List.copyOf) is the honest signature — a good one-line follow-up exercise.
  • Python's tuple (pc, filename) becomes a small Job class; from Java 16 on, record Job(String pc, String filename) {} says the same thing in one line.

        List<Map<String, String>> docs = new ArrayList<>();
        docs.add(Map.of("title", "Clean Code"));

Read it first

As in a3, the Java snippet does not compile yet — SearchPage names a BookSource type nobody has declared. That is task 1. The compiler is doing the same job the marking scheme does.

Your task

  • Declare the target interface (BookSource) that SearchPage is already written against: search(keyword) returning a list, and source_name().
  • Wrap OpenLibraryAPI using an object adapter (composition).
  • Wrap OldCardCatalog using a class adapter (inheritance).
  • The dictionary-unpacking and the string-splitting are the adapters' job. SearchPage must never see a dict or a raw string.
  • Driver: build one of each, put them in a list, and run the same SearchPage.show call on both.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Adaptees: third-party code, NOT modified ----------
class OpenLibraryAPI:
    def fetch(self, keyword):
        print(f"OpenLibraryAPI: querying web service for '{keyword}'")
        return {"docs": [{"title": "Clean Code"}, {"title": "Refactoring"}]}


class OldCardCatalog:
    def lookup(self, keyword):
        print(f"CardCatalog: scanning index cards for '{keyword}'")
        return "Design Patterns;Head First Design Patterns;UML Distilled"


# ---------- Target ----------
class BookSource(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def search(self, keyword):
        """must return a plain list of title strings"""

    @abstractmethod
    def source_name(self):
        pass


# ---------- Object Adapter (composition) ----------
class OpenLibraryObjectAdapter(BookSource):
    def __init__(self, adaptee):
        self.adaptee = adaptee

    def search(self, keyword):
        raw = self.adaptee.fetch(keyword)
        return [doc["title"] for doc in raw["docs"]]

    def source_name(self):
        return "Open Library"


# ---------- Class Adapter (inheritance) ----------
class CardCatalogClassAdapter(BookSource, OldCardCatalog):
    def search(self, keyword):
        raw = self.lookup(keyword)
        return raw.split(";")

    def source_name(self):
        return "Card Catalog"


# ---------- Client ----------
class SearchPage:
    def show(self, source, keyword):
        titles = source.search(keyword)
        name = source.source_name()
        print(f"Results from {name}:")
        for i, title in enumerate(titles, start=1):
            print(f"  {i}. {title}")
        print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    page = SearchPage()

    online = OpenLibraryObjectAdapter(OpenLibraryAPI())
    offline = CardCatalogClassAdapter()

    for source in (online, offline):
        page.show(source, "software design")

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

// ---------- Adaptees: third-party code, NOT modified ----------
class OpenLibraryAPI {
    Map<String, List<Map<String, String>>> fetch(String keyword) {
        System.out.println("OpenLibraryAPI: querying web service for '" + keyword + "'");
        List<Map<String, String>> docs = new ArrayList<>();
        docs.add(Map.of("title", "Clean Code"));
        docs.add(Map.of("title", "Refactoring"));
        return Map.of("docs", docs);
    }
}

class OldCardCatalog {
    String lookup(String keyword) {
        System.out.println("CardCatalog: scanning index cards for '" + keyword + "'");
        return "Design Patterns;Head First Design Patterns;UML Distilled";
    }
}

// ---------- Target ----------
interface BookSource {
    List<String> search(String keyword);        // a plain list of title strings

    String sourceName();
}

// ---------- Object Adapter (composition) ----------
class OpenLibraryObjectAdapter implements BookSource {
    private final OpenLibraryAPI adaptee;

    public OpenLibraryObjectAdapter(OpenLibraryAPI adaptee) {
        this.adaptee = adaptee;
    }

    @Override
    public List<String> search(String keyword) {
        List<String> titles = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Map<String, String> doc : adaptee.fetch(keyword).get("docs")) {
            titles.add(doc.get("title"));           // unpacking lives here
        }
        return titles;
    }

    @Override
    public String sourceName() {
        return "Open Library";
    }
}

// ---------- Class Adapter (inheritance) ----------
class CardCatalogClassAdapter extends OldCardCatalog implements BookSource {
    @Override
    public List<String> search(String keyword) {
        return Arrays.asList(lookup(keyword).split(";"));   // splitting lives here
    }

    @Override
    public String sourceName() {
        return "Card Catalog";
    }
}

// ---------- Client ----------
class SearchPage {
    void show(BookSource source, String keyword) {
        List<String> titles = source.search(keyword);
        String name = source.sourceName();
        System.out.println("Results from " + name + ":");
        for (int i = 0; i < titles.size(); i++) {
            System.out.println("  " + (i + 1) + ". " + titles.get(i));
        }
        System.out.println();
    }
}

public class BookSearchDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SearchPage page = new SearchPage();

        BookSource online = new OpenLibraryObjectAdapter(new OpenLibraryAPI());
        BookSource offline = new CardCatalogClassAdapter();

        for (BookSource source : new BookSource[]{online, offline}) {
            page.show(source, "software design");
        }
    }
}
Output
OpenLibraryAPI: querying web service for 'software design'
Results from Open Library:
  1. Clean Code
  2. Refactoring

CardCatalog: scanning index cards for 'software design'
Results from Card Catalog:
  1. Design Patterns
  2. Head First Design Patterns
  3. UML Distilled

Participants

RoleClass
AdapteesOpenLibraryAPI, OldCardCatalog
TargetBookSource
AdaptersOpenLibraryObjectAdapter, CardCatalogClassAdapter
ClientsSearchPage

Marking points

  • Neither back-end class is edited. Any change there is an automatic deduction.
  • Object adapter holds the adaptee as an attribute; class adapter inherits from BookSource and the adaptee, and calls self.lookup(...) directly.
  • Both search methods return a plain list. If a dict or a raw string escapes into SearchPage, the target contract is broken.
  • SearchPage.show is unchanged and is called identically for both sources.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • The adaptee's return type is where Java gets loud: Map<String, List<Map<String, String>>> is exactly what {"docs": [{"title": ...}]} means, spelled out. Students often meet this shape for the first time when a JSON library hands it to them, and the adapter is precisely the place it should stop.
  • Arrays.asList(...) returns a fixed-size view over the split array — add and remove throw. Use new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(...)) or List.of(...) if the caller may modify it.
  • As in a3, the class adapter is extends OldCardCatalog implements BookSource: Java's single inheritance permits the class adapter only when the target is an interface.

Follow-up answers

1.Tomorrow the library buys a third back-end that is handed to you as an already-created object from a factory you don't control. Which of your two adapter styles can take it, and which cannot?

Only the object adapter. It receives the adaptee instance in its constructor, so any already-built object of a compatible shape can be wrapped. The class adapter binds its adaptee at class-definition time through inheritance — it can only ever create and adapt that one class, never an object handed to it from outside.

Practice — Set BFactory Method

The Result Export Portals

Let the subclass decide what to build

The story

The university exports the same semester result data through three portals: the exam office wants a PDF, the data analytics team wants a CSV, and the student web portal wants HTML.

Every portal follows the exact same export routine: create the report object, announce the title, render the rows, then report the saved filename. That routine never changes. What changes is which kind of report a given portal produces.

Right now the routine carries an if/elif chain, so adding a fourth format means editing the one routine every portal shares. The portal knows when a report must be created; it should not be the place that decides what kind.

class PdfReport:
    def extension(self):
        return "pdf"

    def render(self, rows):
        print("  [PDF] page 1 of 1, letterhead applied")
        for row in rows:
            print(f"    * {row}")


class CsvReport:
    def extension(self):
        return "csv"

    def render(self, rows):
        print("  [CSV] course,marks")
        for row in rows:
            print(f"    {row.replace(' - ', ',')}")


class HtmlReport:
    def extension(self):
        return "html"

    def render(self, rows):
        print("  [HTML] <table>")
        for row in rows:
            print(f"    <tr><td>{row}</td></tr>")
        print("  [HTML] </table>")


class ReportPortal:
    def export(self, kind, title, rows):
        if kind == "pdf":
            report = PdfReport()
        elif kind == "csv":
            report = CsvReport()
        else:
            report = HtmlReport()
        print(f"Exporting '{title}'")
        report.render(rows)
        print(f"  saved as {title.lower().replace(' ', '_')}.{report.extension()}\n")

import java.util.List;

class PdfReport {
    String extension() {
        return "pdf";
    }

    void render(List<String> rows) {
        System.out.println("  [PDF] page 1 of 1, letterhead applied");
        for (String row : rows) {
            System.out.println("    * " + row);
        }
    }
}

class CsvReport {
    String extension() {
        return "csv";
    }

    void render(List<String> rows) {
        System.out.println("  [CSV] course,marks");
        for (String row : rows) {
            System.out.println("    " + row.replace(" - ", ","));
        }
    }
}

class HtmlReport {
    String extension() {
        return "html";
    }

    void render(List<String> rows) {
        System.out.println("  [HTML] <table>");
        for (String row : rows) {
            System.out.println("    <tr><td>" + row + "</td></tr>");
        }
        System.out.println("  [HTML] </table>");
    }
}

class ReportPortal {
    void export(String kind, String title, List<String> rows) {
        // the three report classes share no supertype, so the chain has to
        // carry the rendering call as well as the choice
        System.out.println("Exporting '" + title + "'");
        String ext;
        if (kind.equals("pdf")) {
            PdfReport report = new PdfReport();
            report.render(rows);
            ext = report.extension();
        } else if (kind.equals("csv")) {
            CsvReport report = new CsvReport();
            report.render(rows);
            ext = report.extension();
        } else {
            HtmlReport report = new HtmlReport();
            report.render(rows);
            ext = report.extension();
        }
        System.out.println("  saved as " + title.toLowerCase().replace(' ', '_') + "." + ext + "\n");
    }
}

Your task

  • Give the three report classes a common product interface.
  • Turn ReportPortal into the creator: export keeps the shared routine, but the object it works on comes from an abstract factory method.
  • Write one concrete creator per portal (ExamOfficePortal, DataAnalyticsPortal, StudentWebPortal). The if/elif chain must disappear completely, and export must no longer take a kind argument.
  • Driver: put one of each portal in a list and export the same two rows through each.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Product ----------
class Report(ABC):
    def __init__(self, rows):           # every product is built with its data
        self.rows = rows

    @abstractmethod
    def extension(self):
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def render(self):
        pass


# ---------- Concrete Products ----------
class PdfReport(Report):
    def extension(self):
        return "pdf"

    def render(self):
        print("  [PDF] page 1 of 1, letterhead applied")
        for row in self.rows:
            print(f"    * {row}")


class CsvReport(Report):
    def extension(self):
        return "csv"

    def render(self):
        print("  [CSV] course,marks")
        for row in self.rows:
            cells = row.replace(' - ', ',')
            print(f"    {cells}")


class HtmlReport(Report):
    def extension(self):
        return "html"

    def render(self):
        print("  [HTML] <table>")
        for row in self.rows:
            print(f"    <tr><td>{row}</td></tr>")
        print("  [HTML] </table>")


# ---------- Creator ----------
class ReportPortal(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def create_report(self, rows):    # the factory method
        pass

    def export(self, title, rows):    # the template method
        report = self.create_report(rows)
        print(f"Exporting '{title}'")
        report.render()
        slug = title.lower().replace(' ', '_')
        extension = report.extension()
        print(f"  saved as {slug}.{extension}\n")


# ---------- Concrete Creators ----------
class ExamOfficePortal(ReportPortal):
    def create_report(self, rows):
        return PdfReport(rows)


class DataAnalyticsPortal(ReportPortal):
    def create_report(self, rows):
        return CsvReport(rows)


class StudentWebPortal(ReportPortal):
    def create_report(self, rows):
        return HtmlReport(rows)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    rows = ["CSE470 - 87", "CSE471 - 91"]
    portals = [ExamOfficePortal(), DataAnalyticsPortal(), StudentWebPortal()]

    for portal in portals:
        portal.export("Spring Result", rows)

import java.util.List;

// ---------- Product ----------
abstract class Report {
    protected final List<String> rows;          // every product is built with its data

    protected Report(List<String> rows) {
        this.rows = rows;
    }

    public abstract String extension();

    public abstract void render();
}

// ---------- Concrete Products ----------
class PdfReport extends Report {
    public PdfReport(List<String> rows) {
        super(rows);
    }

    @Override
    public String extension() {
        return "pdf";
    }

    @Override
    public void render() {
        System.out.println("  [PDF] page 1 of 1, letterhead applied");
        for (String row : rows) {
            System.out.println("    * " + row);
        }
    }
}

class CsvReport extends Report {
    public CsvReport(List<String> rows) {
        super(rows);
    }

    @Override
    public String extension() {
        return "csv";
    }

    @Override
    public void render() {
        System.out.println("  [CSV] course,marks");
        for (String row : rows) {
            String cells = row.replace(" - ", ",");
            System.out.println("    " + cells);
        }
    }
}

class HtmlReport extends Report {
    public HtmlReport(List<String> rows) {
        super(rows);
    }

    @Override
    public String extension() {
        return "html";
    }

    @Override
    public void render() {
        System.out.println("  [HTML] <table>");
        for (String row : rows) {
            System.out.println("    <tr><td>" + row + "</td></tr>");
        }
        System.out.println("  [HTML] </table>");
    }
}

// ---------- Creator ----------
abstract class ReportPortal {
    protected abstract Report createReport(List<String> rows);  // the factory method

    public void export(String title, List<String> rows) {       // the template method
        Report report = createReport(rows);
        System.out.println("Exporting '" + title + "'");
        report.render();
        String slug = title.toLowerCase().replace(' ', '_');
        String extension = report.extension();
        System.out.println("  saved as " + slug + "." + extension + "\n");
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Creators ----------
class ExamOfficePortal extends ReportPortal {
    @Override
    protected Report createReport(List<String> rows) {
        return new PdfReport(rows);
    }
}

class DataAnalyticsPortal extends ReportPortal {
    @Override
    protected Report createReport(List<String> rows) {
        return new CsvReport(rows);
    }
}

class StudentWebPortal extends ReportPortal {
    @Override
    protected Report createReport(List<String> rows) {
        return new HtmlReport(rows);
    }
}

public class ResultExportDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<String> rows = List.of("CSE470 - 87", "CSE471 - 91");
        ReportPortal[] portals = {
            new ExamOfficePortal(), new DataAnalyticsPortal(), new StudentWebPortal()
        };

        for (ReportPortal portal : portals) {
            portal.export("Spring Result", rows);
        }
    }
}

Participants

RoleClass
ProductReport
Concrete ProductsPdfReport, CsvReport, HtmlReport
CreatorReportPortal
Concrete CreatorsExamOfficePortal, DataAnalyticsPortal, StudentWebPortal

Marking points

  • create_report is abstract on ReportPortal and overridden in each subclass.
  • export keeps the invariant routine and calls self.create_report(rows) — it never names a concrete report class, and it no longer takes a kind argument.
  • No if/elif on a type string anywhere.
  • Driver treats all three portals through the base type, passing the same rows.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • title.toLowerCase().replace(' ', '_') — the char overload of replace, not the String one. Also note toLowerCase() is locale-sensitive: in a Turkish locale "I" lowercases to a dotless ı. For identifiers, toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) is the correct call.
  • The creator is an abstract class, not an interface, because export is concrete shared behaviour — the whole point of Factory Method is that the base owns the routine. (Java 8+ default methods blur this, but an abstract class is the honest expression of “subclasses fill in one hole”.)
  • Compare with the given Java: there, ext has to be declared outside the chain and every branch repeats render. The pattern removes the duplication that the type system was already complaining about.

Follow-up answers

1.The accounts department now wants a plain-text export. List exactly what you add and what you edit. Compare with the given code.

Two additions — a TextReport product and an AccountsPortal creator. Nothing existing is edited. In the given code, export itself had to be reopened, which is exactly the closed-for-modification violation the pattern removes.

Combined patternsSingletonObserver

Campus Alert Hub

One class, two roles

The story

The university is building one campus-wide alert system.

There must be exactly one alert hub for the whole campus, and every module that needs it — the facilities desk, the security office, anything added later — must end up talking to that same hub. Two hubs would be a disaster: a device registered through one would never hear an alert raised through the other. The hub must also not boot when the software starts; it should come up the first time some module actually reaches for it.

Attached to the hub are the alert devices: lobby notice screens, students' mobile apps, and a compliance archive that silently records every alert. When security raises an alert, every device currently attached must be told immediately — no device should have to keep polling the hub asking whether anything happened. Devices are installed and removed while the system is running, and the hub has no idea how many are attached at any moment.

The hub must not contain any device-specific logic. All it knows is that whatever is attached can be told “an alert was raised.”

class AlertHub:
    def __init__(self):
        print("Booting campus alert hub...")
        self.devices = []
        self.level = None
        self.latest = None

    def raise_alert(self, level, text):
        self.level = level
        self.latest = text


class NoticeScreen:
    def __init__(self, location):
        self.location = location

    def check(self, hub):
        # the screen has to come and ask, every single time
        print(f"[Screen-{self.location}] {hub.level}: {hub.latest}")


class FacilitiesDesk:
    def install(self, device):
        hub = AlertHub()
        hub.devices.append(device)
        print(f"installed {type(device).__name__}")


class SecurityOffice:
    def broadcast(self, level, text):
        hub = AlertHub()
        hub.raise_alert(level, text)

        this.latest = text;

        this.location = location;

    void check(AlertHub hub) {
        // the screen has to come and ask, every single time
        System.out.println("[Screen-" + location + "] " + hub.level + ": " + hub.latest);
    }

    void install(Object device) {

        hub.devices.add(device);
        System.out.println("installed " + device.getClass().getSimpleName());

        AlertHub hub = new AlertHub();
        hub.raiseAlert(level, text);

Read it first

Run this as it stands and you will see the problem twice over: the boot message prints once per module, and the screen installed by the facilities desk never hears the alert the security office raised — it was added to a completely different hub object.

Your task

  1. Guarantee a single hub. Every AlertHub() call must hand back the same object, created lazily. FacilitiesDesk and SecurityOffice must keep calling AlertHub() exactly as they do now — you may not edit them to accept a hub as an argument.
  2. Make the hub push, not the devices poll. Introduce the observer interface and the subject machinery (attach, detach, notify), and call notify() from inside raise_alert.
  3. Add two more device types beyond NoticeScreen — a MobileApp and an AlertArchive — to prove the hub is not tied to any one device class.
  4. Support removal. Add an uninstall to the facilities desk; a removed device must produce no output on the next alert.
  5. Driver: install three devices through the facilities desk, broadcast one alert through the security office, uninstall one device, broadcast a second alert, then print an identity check on the hub.

Where this one goes wrong

__init__ runs on every AlertHub() call, so if the observer list is initialised in the wrong place, every module that touches the hub silently wipes the device registry — and your alerts reach nobody.

Expected shape of the output

--- campus opening, hub not booted yet ---
Booting campus alert hub...
installed NoticeScreen
installed MobileApp
installed AlertArchive
[Screen-UB4-Lobby] DRILL: Fire drill at 3 PM
[App/Zobayer] push notification - Fire drill at 3 PM (DRILL)
[Archive] alert #1 stored
removed MobileApp
[Screen-UB4-Lobby] URGENT: Building closing early
[Archive] alert #2 stored
one hub? True

The boot message appears once, and after the opening line. The devices were registered through one module and notified because of an alert raised in another — that is the point of the whole exercise.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Observer interface ----------
class Observer(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def update(self, subject):
        pass


# ---------- Subject ----------
class Subject:
    def __init__(self):
        self._observers = []

    def attach(self, observer):
        self._observers.append(observer)

    def detach(self, observer):
        if observer in self._observers:
            self._observers.remove(observer)

    def notify(self):
        for observer in self._observers:
            observer.update(self)


# ---------- Singleton + Concrete Subject ----------
class AlertHub(Subject):
    _instance = None

    def __new__(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:                      # lazy creation
            print("Booting campus alert hub...")
            cls._instance = super(AlertHub, cls).__new__(cls)
        return cls._instance

    def __init__(self):
        if hasattr(self, "_level"):                    # already set up: do it once
            return
        super().__init__()                             # Subject: self._observers = []
        self._level = None
        self._latest = None

    def raise_alert(self, level, text):
        self._level = level
        self._latest = text
        self.notify()

    def get_level(self):
        return self._level

    def get_latest(self):
        return self._latest


# ---------- Concrete Observers ----------
class NoticeScreen(Observer):
    def __init__(self, location):
        self.location = location

    def update(self, subject):
        level = subject.get_level()
        text = subject.get_latest()
        print(f"[Screen-{self.location}] {level}: {text}")


class MobileApp(Observer):
    def __init__(self, owner):
        self.owner = owner

    def update(self, subject):
        level = subject.get_level()
        text = subject.get_latest()
        print(f"[App/{self.owner}] push notification - {text} ({level})")


class AlertArchive(Observer):
    def __init__(self):
        self.log = []

    def update(self, subject):
        level = subject.get_level()
        text = subject.get_latest()
        self.log.append(f"{level}: {text}")
        count = len(self.log)
        print(f"[Archive] alert #{count} stored")


# ---------- Clients: each one asks for the hub independently ----------
class FacilitiesDesk:
    def install(self, device):
        AlertHub().attach(device)
        kind = type(device).__name__
        print(f"installed {kind}")

    def uninstall(self, device):
        AlertHub().detach(device)
        kind = type(device).__name__
        print(f"removed {kind}")


class SecurityOffice:
    def broadcast(self, level, text):
        AlertHub().raise_alert(level, text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- campus opening, hub not booted yet ---")

    facilities = FacilitiesDesk()
    security = SecurityOffice()

    screen = NoticeScreen("UB4-Lobby")
    app = MobileApp("Zobayer")
    archive = AlertArchive()

    facilities.install(screen)
    facilities.install(app)
    facilities.install(archive)

    security.broadcast("DRILL", "Fire drill at 3 PM")

    facilities.uninstall(app)
    security.broadcast("URGENT", "Building closing early")

    print("one hub?", AlertHub() is AlertHub())

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

// ---------- Observer interface ----------
interface Observer {
    void update(Subject subject);
}

// ---------- Subject ----------
class Subject {
    private final List<Observer> observers = new ArrayList<>();

    public void attach(Observer observer) {
        observers.add(observer);
    }

    public void detach(Observer observer) {
        observers.remove(observer);
    }

    public void notifyObservers() {                 // notify() is final on Object
        for (Observer observer : new ArrayList<>(observers)) {
            observer.update(this);
        }
    }
}

// ---------- Singleton + Concrete Subject ----------
class AlertHub extends Subject {
    private static AlertHub instance;
    private String level;
    private String latest;

    private AlertHub() {                            // runs exactly once, ever
        System.out.println("Booting campus alert hub...");
    }

    public static AlertHub getInstance() {          // lazy creation
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new AlertHub();
        }
        return instance;
    }

    public void raiseAlert(String level, String text) {
        this.level = level;
        this.latest = text;
        notifyObservers();
    }

    public String getLevel() {
        return level;
    }

    public String getLatest() {
        return latest;
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Observers ----------
class NoticeScreen implements Observer {
    private final String location;

    public NoticeScreen(String location) {
        this.location = location;
    }

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        AlertHub hub = (AlertHub) subject;
        String level = hub.getLevel();
        String text = hub.getLatest();
        System.out.println("[Screen-" + location + "] " + level + ": " + text);
    }
}

class MobileApp implements Observer {
    private final String owner;

    public MobileApp(String owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        AlertHub hub = (AlertHub) subject;
        String level = hub.getLevel();
        String text = hub.getLatest();
        System.out.println("[App/" + owner + "] push notification - "
                + text + " (" + level + ")");
    }
}

class AlertArchive implements Observer {
    private final List<String> log = new ArrayList<>();

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        AlertHub hub = (AlertHub) subject;
        String level = hub.getLevel();
        String text = hub.getLatest();
        log.add(level + ": " + text);
        int count = log.size();
        System.out.println("[Archive] alert #" + count + " stored");
    }
}

// ---------- Clients: each one asks for the hub independently ----------
class FacilitiesDesk {
    public void install(Observer device) {
        AlertHub.getInstance().attach(device);
        String kind = device.getClass().getSimpleName();
        System.out.println("installed " + kind);
    }

    public void uninstall(Observer device) {
        AlertHub.getInstance().detach(device);
        String kind = device.getClass().getSimpleName();
        System.out.println("removed " + kind);
    }
}

class SecurityOffice {
    public void broadcast(String level, String text) {
        AlertHub.getInstance().raiseAlert(level, text);
    }
}

public class AlertHubDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("--- campus opening, hub not booted yet ---");

        FacilitiesDesk facilities = new FacilitiesDesk();
        SecurityOffice security = new SecurityOffice();

        NoticeScreen screen = new NoticeScreen("UB4-Lobby");
        MobileApp app = new MobileApp("Zobayer");
        AlertArchive archive = new AlertArchive();

        facilities.install(screen);
        facilities.install(app);
        facilities.install(archive);

        security.broadcast("DRILL", "Fire drill at 3 PM");

        facilities.uninstall(app);
        security.broadcast("URGENT", "Building closing early");

        System.out.println("one hub? " + (AlertHub.getInstance() == AlertHub.getInstance()));
    }
}

Participants

RoleClass
ObserverObserver
SubjectSubject
Concrete SubjectAlertHub
Concrete ObserversNoticeScreen, MobileApp, AlertArchive
SingletonAlertHub
ClientsFacilitiesDesk, SecurityOffice

The overlap

AlertHub fills two rows of that table. It is the singleton and the concrete subject — the class owns both the lifecycle and the notification. That doubling-up is normal when the one shared object is also the thing that broadcasts, and it is worth naming out loud.

Marking points

  • __new__ overridden, _instance a class attribute, guard is if cls._instance is None — that is what makes it lazy. Boot message prints once, after the opening line.
  • _observers is initialised inside the __new__ guard, not in an __init__. This is the crux of the combined problem: Subject.__init__ doing self._observers = [] would run on every AlertHub() call and wipe the registry, so the security office's alert would reach nobody even though the devices were installed. Note that the reference solution therefore gives Subject no __init__ at all.
  • notify() is called from inside raise_alert, not from the driver.
  • AlertHub never names NoticeScreen, MobileApp or AlertArchive anywhere.
  • FacilitiesDesk and SecurityOffice are unedited in shape — they still call AlertHub() with no arguments. A solution that passes the hub in as a constructor argument has solved the problem by removing it.
  • detach works: the uninstalled app produces no output on the second alert.
  • Identity check prints True.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • The Python trap does not exist in Java. Because a private constructor runs only when an object is really created, the field initialiser private final List<Observer> observers = new ArrayList<>() fires exactly once, and AlertHub needs no constructor guard at all. Python calls __init__ on every AlertHub() — __new__ hands back the same object, then __init__ runs again and would reset self._observers to an empty list, silently unsubscribing everybody. That is why the Python __init__ starts with if hasattr(self, "_level"): return. Worth showing side by side: the same design, one language needing a guard the other does not.
  • In exchange, Java forces the clients to change to AlertHub.getInstance() — the Python brief's “don't edit the clients” rule cannot be honoured.
  • device.getClass().getSimpleName() is the direct equivalent of type(device).__name__.
  • detach during notifyObservers() would throw ConcurrentModificationException without the defensive copy. The driver here detaches between alerts, so it never fires — which is exactly the kind of bug that ships.

Follow-up answers

1.Using the participant names from both patterns, list every role AlertHub plays. Why do two roles land on one class here?

AlertHub is the Singleton and, at the same time, the Concrete Subject. From the singleton it takes _instance and the lazy creation inside __new__; from the observer pattern it takes the observer list and attach/detach/notify, inherited from Subject. The two roles land together because the story asks for exactly one hub and asks that same hub to broadcast — the thing that must be unique is the thing that must notify. The point of the question is to see that two participant tables can name the same class.

2.The facilities desk and the security office each call AlertHub() separately. If the hub were not a singleton, describe exactly which line of the expected output disappears first.

[Screen-UB4-Lobby] DRILL: Fire drill at 3 PM and both other device lines — the first broadcast would print nothing at all, because the devices sit on the facilities desk's hub while raise_alert fires on the security office's hub.

Combined patternsAdapterObserver

Flood Warning Station

The target interface is the observer interface

The story

A river monitoring station takes a water-level reading every few minutes. The moment a new reading arrives, every warning device attached to the station must react immediately — nothing should sit in a loop asking the station whether the level changed. Devices are attached and removed while the station is running (a siren goes for maintenance, a new display is installed), and the station has no idea how many are listening at any moment.

Here is the difficulty. The station's own mobile app was written by your team and can be told whatever you like. The other two devices are field hardware you cannot modify, and neither of them speaks the station's language:

  • The siren does not understand water levels at all. It only accepts a duration in seconds — so somebody has to translate a severity into “how long to wail”.
  • The LED board needs three calls in a fixed order — set line 1, set line 2, commit — and each line must be uppercase and at most 16 characters. Anything longer is simply cut.

The station must not contain a single line of siren-specific or board-specific logic. All it knows is that whatever is attached can be told “a new reading arrived”.

class SirenController:
    def activate(self, seconds):
        print(f"  Siren: wailing for {seconds}s")

    def deactivate(self):
        print("  Siren: silent")


class LegacyLedBoard:
    def set_line1(self, text):
        self._l1 = text

    def set_line2(self, text):
        self._l2 = text

    def commit(self):
        print(f"  LED: |{self._l1:<16}|")
        print(f"  LED: |{self._l2:<16}|")


# ---- your side ----
class WaterLevelStation:
    def __init__(self, river, siren, board):
        self.river = river
        self.level = 0.0
        self.siren = siren          # exactly two devices, forever
        self.board = board

    def record_level(self, meters):
        self.level = meters
        print(f"{self.river}: reading {meters} m")

        if meters >= 6.0:
            self.siren.activate(30)
        elif meters >= 4.5:
            self.siren.activate(10)
        else:
            self.siren.deactivate()

        self.board.set_line1(self.river.upper()[:16])
        self.board.set_line2(f"{meters}M"[:16])
        self.board.commit()

// ---- field hardware: DO NOT MODIFY these two classes ----
class SirenController {
    void activate(int seconds) {
        System.out.println("  Siren: wailing for " + seconds + "s");
    }

    void deactivate() {
        System.out.println("  Siren: silent");

class LegacyLedBoard {
    private String l1;
    private String l2;

    void setLine1(String text) {
        this.l1 = text;
    }

    void setLine2(String text) {
        this.l2 = text;
    }

    void commit() {
        System.out.printf("  LED: |%-16s|%n", l1);
        System.out.printf("  LED: |%-16s|%n", l2);
    }
}

// ---- your side ----
class WaterLevelStation {
    String river;
    double level = 0.0;
    SirenController siren;          // exactly two devices, forever
    LegacyLedBoard board;

    WaterLevelStation(String river, SirenController siren, LegacyLedBoard board) {
        this.river = river;
        this.siren = siren;
        this.board = board;
    }

    void recordLevel(double meters) {
        this.level = meters;
        System.out.println(river + ": reading " + meters + " m");

        if (meters >= 6.0) {
            siren.activate(30);
        } else if (meters >= 4.5) {
            siren.activate(10);
        } else {
            siren.deactivate();
        }

        String name = river.toUpperCase();
        board.setLine1(name.length() > 16 ? name.substring(0, 16) : name);
        board.setLine2(meters + "M");
        board.commit();
    }
}

Read it first

Read record_level carefully — it has two separate faults living in one method. It is welded to exactly two devices that were handed to its constructor, and it knows both of their private vocabularies. Each pattern you apply removes one of them.

Your task

  1. Declare the observer interface with a single update(subject) method, and add the subject machinery (attach, detach, notify) to the station. record_level must call notify().
  2. Give the station a severity rule it can be asked for: get_level() returns the reading and get_severity() returns a severity string — DANGER at 6.0 m and above, WARNING at 4.5 m and above, otherwise NORMAL. The severity logic belongs to the station; how a device reacts to it does not.
  3. Adapt the two field devices so they can be attached as observers. Neither has an update method, and neither ever will. Wrap each of them in an object adapter — the adapter holds the device in an adaptee field and calls it. The severity-to-duration mapping and the uppercase/truncate/three-call formatting each live inside their own adapter — not in the station, and not in the driver.
  4. Add one native observer — a MobileApp that implements the observer interface directly, with no adapter. Your station must treat it identically to the two adapted devices.
  5. Driver: attach all three, record a normal reading, record a warning reading, detach the app, record a danger reading.

Expected shape of the output

Jamuna at Sirajganj: reading 3.2 m
  Siren: silent
  LED: |JAMUNA AT SIRAJG|
  LED: |3.2M NORMAL     |
  App/Zobayer: NORMAL - water at 3.2 m
Jamuna at Sirajganj: reading 5.0 m
  Siren: wailing for 10s
  LED: |JAMUNA AT SIRAJG|
  LED: |5.0M WARNING    |
  App/Zobayer: WARNING - water at 5.0 m
Jamuna at Sirajganj: reading 6.5 m
  Siren: wailing for 30s
  LED: |JAMUNA AT SIRAJG|
  LED: |6.5M DANGER     |

The river name is genuinely longer than 16 characters — the board cutting it off is correct behaviour, and it should be your adapter doing the cutting.

Follow-up questions (2–3 lines each)

Which fault in the given record_level did the observer pattern remove, and which did the adapter remove? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?
The MobileApp needed no adapter, while the siren did. What exactly decides whether a device needs one?
Next season the station adds a rainfall sensor whose readings should also drive the same three devices. What do you add, and what do you edit?

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Adaptees: vendor devices, NOT modified ----------
class SirenController:
    def activate(self, seconds):
        print(f"  Siren: wailing for {seconds}s")

    def deactivate(self):
        print("  Siren: silent")


class LegacyLedBoard:
    def set_line1(self, text):
        self._l1 = text

    def set_line2(self, text):
        self._l2 = text

    def commit(self):
        print(f"  LED: |{self._l1:<16}|")
        print(f"  LED: |{self._l2:<16}|")


# ---------- Target / Observer ----------
class Observer(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def update(self, subject):
        pass


# ---------- Subject ----------
class Subject:
    def __init__(self):
        self._observers = []

    def attach(self, observer):
        self._observers.append(observer)

    def detach(self, observer):
        if observer in self._observers:
            self._observers.remove(observer)

    def notify(self):
        for observer in self._observers:
            observer.update(self)


# ---------- Concrete Subject ----------
class WaterLevelStation(Subject):
    def __init__(self, river):
        super().__init__()
        self._river = river
        self._level = 0.0

    def record_level(self, meters):
        self._level = meters
        print(f"{self._river}: reading {meters} m")
        self.notify()

    def get_river(self):
        return self._river

    def get_level(self):
        return self._level

    def get_severity(self):                # the rule lives here, once
        if self._level >= 6.0:
            return "DANGER"
        if self._level >= 4.5:
            return "WARNING"
        return "NORMAL"


# ---------- Adapters as Observers (object adapters) ----------
class SirenAdapter(Observer):
    def __init__(self, adaptee):
        self.adaptee = adaptee

    def update(self, subject):
        severity = subject.get_severity()
        if severity == "DANGER":
            self.adaptee.activate(30)          # severity -> duration
        elif severity == "WARNING":
            self.adaptee.activate(10)
        else:
            self.adaptee.deactivate()


class LedBoardAdapter(Observer):
    def __init__(self, adaptee):
        self.adaptee = adaptee

    def update(self, subject):
        level = subject.get_level()
        severity = subject.get_severity()
        river = subject.get_river()
        self.adaptee.set_line1(river.upper()[:16])                 # one update ->
        self.adaptee.set_line2(f"{level}M {severity}"[:16])        # three adaptee
        self.adaptee.commit()                                      # calls


# ---------- Native Observer, no adapter needed ----------
class MobileApp(Observer):
    def __init__(self, owner):
        self.owner = owner

    def update(self, subject):
        level = subject.get_level()
        severity = subject.get_severity()
        print(f"  App/{self.owner}: {severity} - water at {level} m")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    station = WaterLevelStation("Jamuna at Sirajganj")

    siren = SirenAdapter(SirenController())
    board = LedBoardAdapter(LegacyLedBoard())
    app = MobileApp("Zobayer")

    station.attach(siren)
    station.attach(board)
    station.attach(app)

    station.record_level(3.2)
    station.record_level(5.0)

    station.detach(app)
    station.record_level(6.5)

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

// ---------- Adaptees: vendor devices, NOT modified ----------
class SirenController {
    void activate(int seconds) {
        System.out.println("  Siren: wailing for " + seconds + "s");
    }

    void deactivate() {
        System.out.println("  Siren: silent");
    }
}

class LegacyLedBoard {
    private String l1;
    private String l2;

    void setLine1(String text) {
        this.l1 = text;
    }

    void setLine2(String text) {
        this.l2 = text;
    }

    void commit() {
        System.out.printf("  LED: |%-16s|%n", l1);
        System.out.printf("  LED: |%-16s|%n", l2);
    }
}

// ---------- Target / Observer ----------
interface Observer {
    void update(Subject subject);
}

// ---------- Subject ----------
class Subject {
    private final List<Observer> observers = new ArrayList<>();

    public void attach(Observer observer) {
        observers.add(observer);
    }

    public void detach(Observer observer) {
        observers.remove(observer);
    }

    public void notifyObservers() {
        for (Observer observer : new ArrayList<>(observers)) {
            observer.update(this);
        }
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Subject ----------
class WaterLevelStation extends Subject {
    private final String river;
    private double level = 0.0;

    public WaterLevelStation(String river) {
        this.river = river;
    }

    public void recordLevel(double meters) {
        this.level = meters;
        System.out.println(river + ": reading " + meters + " m");
        notifyObservers();
    }

    public String getRiver() {
        return river;
    }

    public double getLevel() {
        return level;
    }

    public String getSeverity() {              // the rule lives here, once
        if (level >= 6.0) {
            return "DANGER";
        }
        if (level >= 4.5) {
            return "WARNING";
        }
        return "NORMAL";
    }
}

// ---------- Adapters as Observers (object adapters) ----------
class SirenAdapter implements Observer {
    private final SirenController adaptee;

    public SirenAdapter(SirenController adaptee) {
        this.adaptee = adaptee;
    }

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        String severity = ((WaterLevelStation) subject).getSeverity();
        if (severity.equals("DANGER")) {
            adaptee.activate(30);              // severity -> duration
        } else if (severity.equals("WARNING")) {
            adaptee.activate(10);
        } else {
            adaptee.deactivate();
        }
    }
}

class LedBoardAdapter implements Observer {
    private final LegacyLedBoard adaptee;

    public LedBoardAdapter(LegacyLedBoard adaptee) {
        this.adaptee = adaptee;
    }

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        WaterLevelStation station = (WaterLevelStation) subject;
        double level = station.getLevel();
        String severity = station.getSeverity();
        String river = station.getRiver();
        adaptee.setLine1(clip(river.toUpperCase()));            // one update ->
        adaptee.setLine2(clip(level + "M " + severity));        // three adaptee
        adaptee.commit();                                       // calls
    }

    private static String clip(String text) {
        return text.length() > 16 ? text.substring(0, 16) : text;
    }
}

// ---------- Native Observer, no adapter needed ----------
class MobileApp implements Observer {
    private final String owner;

    public MobileApp(String owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    @Override
    public void update(Subject subject) {
        WaterLevelStation station = (WaterLevelStation) subject;
        double level = station.getLevel();
        String severity = station.getSeverity();
        System.out.println("  App/" + owner + ": " + severity
                + " - water at " + level + " m");
    }
}

public class FloodStationDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        WaterLevelStation station = new WaterLevelStation("Jamuna at Sirajganj");

        SirenAdapter siren = new SirenAdapter(new SirenController());
        LedBoardAdapter board = new LedBoardAdapter(new LegacyLedBoard());
        MobileApp app = new MobileApp("Zobayer");

        station.attach(siren);
        station.attach(board);
        station.attach(app);

        station.recordLevel(3.2);
        station.recordLevel(5.0);

        station.detach(app);
        station.recordLevel(6.5);
    }
}

AdapteesSirenController, LegacyLedBoard
TargetObserver
ObserverObserver

The overlap

Two overlaps, and both are the point. Observer is also the Target — the interface the vendors are adapted to is the interface the subject notifies through. The adapters are also the concrete observers — SirenAdapter wraps SirenController and gets update called on it. MobileApp shows the contrast: something already speaking the target interface needs no adapter at all.

Marking points

  • Neither field-hardware class is edited. Any change there is an automatic deduction.
  • WaterLevelStation contains no activate, deactivate, set_line1, or commit call, and never names a device class. If any vendor vocabulary survives in the station, the adapter half was not applied.
  • notify() is called from inside record_level, not from the driver.
  • record_level no longer takes devices in the constructor; the station's __init__ takes only the river.
  • Severity is computed once, in the station's get_severity(). If each adapter re-derives it from the raw level with its own thresholds, the rule is duplicated three ways and will drift — worth a deduction even though the output is identical.
  • The severity-to-duration mapping is inside SirenAdapter; the uppercase/[:16]/three-call sequence is inside LedBoardAdapter.
  • SirenAdapter holds its adaptee as an attribute; LedBoardAdapter inherits from Observer and LegacyLedBoard, calling self.set_line1(...) directly.
  • detach works: the app produces no output on the third reading.
  • All three devices are attached and notified through the same calls — the station cannot tell which are adapted.
  • A common near-miss: keeping the siren and board as plain attributes on the station and adding observers only for the app. That produces the same output for this driver but leaves the original coupling untouched — check the station's __init__ and its notify loop, not the printed result.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • String.format/printf with %-16s is the direct translation of Python's {:<16}. %n rather than \n gives the platform line separator.
  • Python's text[:16] never fails on a short string; Java's substring(0, 16) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The clip helper exists purely to make that safe — a small reminder that slicing is one of the places Python quietly does the right thing.
  • Both adapters here are object adapters: they hold the vendor device in an adaptee field. Java would also allow class LedBoardAdapter extends LegacyLedBoard implements Observer — the class-adapter form — because Observer is an interface and the single inheritance slot is free. That variant is drilled in Checkout with Two Payment Vendors and Two Book Search Back-ends; here both adapters keep the same shape so the Observer half is the only thing that changes.

Follow-up answers

1.Which fault in the given record_level did the observer pattern remove, and which did the adapter remove? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?

The observer pattern removed the coupling fault — the station no longer holds two fixed devices and no longer decides who hears about a reading; devices come and go at runtime. The adapter removed the vocabulary fault — the station no longer knows that a siren takes seconds or that a board needs three calls. Either alone leaves the other: observers alone cannot help, because neither device has an update method to call, so the station would still be reaching into vendor APIs from inside its notify loop; adapters alone leave the station welded to exactly the two devices it was constructed with.

2.The MobileApp needed no adapter, while the siren did. What exactly decides whether a device needs one?

Whether it already conforms to the target interface. MobileApp was written by the team, so it was simply made an Observer from the start. The siren is fixed, external, and shaped differently, so a wrapper is the only way to give it the shape the subject requires. The rule of thumb: adapt what you cannot change, implement directly what you can.

3.Next season the station adds a rainfall sensor whose readings should also drive the same three devices. What do you add, and what do you edit?

Add a RainfallSensor as a second concrete subject over the same Subject base — it inherits attach, detach and notify unchanged. The three devices are attached to it and are not edited at all. It is the same shape as two concrete celebrities sharing one Celebrity base in the lecture. The one thing to check: the observers call back into the subject to read the state — subject.get_severity(), exactly as Fan.update calls celebrity.get_state() — so the new subject must offer that method too.

Combined patternsAdapterFactory Method

The Upload Service

The Target and the Product are one type

The story

The university's file upload service saves a student's submission and then shows a link to it. The routine is always the same: put the file somewhere, then hand back a link. That routine never changes.

What changes is where the file goes. The developer laptops write to local disk, the cloud deployment pushes to DropBox, and the campus data centre still runs an old FTP server. A given deployment only ever uses one of them, and it is decided when that deployment is set up — the upload service knows when a file must be stored, not which back-end stores it.

Each back-end arrives as a vendor SDK you cannot edit, and no two of them agree on anything. Their method names differ, DropBox returns a share URL while local disk returns a filesystem path, and the FTP module needs three calls in a fixed order — open, transfer, close — where the others need one.

Right now the upload routine carries an if/elif chain and calls each vendor's methods by name inside it, so adding a fourth back-end means reopening the one routine every deployment shares.

class LocalDisk:
    def write(self, path, content):

        print("  FTP: connection opened")

    def put(self, filename, data):
        print(f"  FTP: PUT {filename} ({len(data)} bytes)")

    def quit(self):

    def url(self, filename):

# ---- your side ----
class UploadService:

        print(f"Storing {filename}")

            disk = LocalDisk()
            disk.write(filename, content)
            print(f"  available at {disk.path_of(filename)}\n")
        elif mode == "cloud":
            box = DropBoxSDK()
            box.upload_file(filename, content)
            print(f"  available at {box.share_link(filename)}\n")
        else:
            ftp = CampusFTP()
            ftp.connect()
            ftp.put(filename, content)
            ftp.quit()
            print(f"  available at {ftp.url(filename)}\n")

Read it first

Notice that this one method has two separate faults: it decides which back-end to build, and it also knows the private vocabulary of all three. Each pattern you apply removes one of them.

Your task

  1. Declare the common interface — call it Storage, with save(filename, content) and link(filename). This one interface plays a double role: it is the interface the vendors are being adapted to, and it is also the type the creator hands back. Say so in your comment.
  2. Wrap each vendor in an object adapter — the adapter holds the vendor object in an adaptee field and calls it. All three look the same; CampusFTP's adapter is the interesting one, because that is where the three-call open/transfer/close sequence gets folded into a single save.
  3. Turn UploadService into the creator. store keeps the shared routine, but the object it works on comes from an abstract factory method. store must no longer take a mode argument, and no vendor class name may appear inside it.
  4. Write one concrete creator per deployment — DevUploadService, CloudUploadService, CampusUploadService. The if/elif chain must disappear completely.
  5. Driver: put one of each service in a list and store the same file through each. Use "x" * 2048 as the file content.

Expected shape of the output

Storing thesis.pdf
  LocalDisk: wrote 2048 bytes to ./thesis.pdf
  available at file:///var/data/thesis.pdf

Storing thesis.pdf
  DropBox: uploaded thesis.pdf (2048 bytes)
  available at https://dropbox.com/s/thesis.pdf

Storing thesis.pdf
  FTP: connection opened
  FTP: PUT thesis.pdf (2048 bytes)
  FTP: connection closed
  available at ftp://campus.edu/pub/thesis.pdf

Which fault in the given store did the adapter remove, and which did the factory method remove? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?
The FTP adapter turns one call into three. Why is that the adapter's job and not the upload service's?
Google Drive is added next year, with yet another SDK. List exactly what you add and what you edit. Compare with the given code.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Adaptees: vendor SDKs, NOT modified ----------
class LocalDisk:
    def write(self, path, content):
        size = len(content)
        print(f"  LocalDisk: wrote {size} bytes to ./{path}")

    def path_of(self, path):
        return f"file:///var/data/{path}"


class DropBoxSDK:
    def upload_file(self, filename, blob):
        size = len(blob)
        print(f"  DropBox: uploaded {filename} ({size} bytes)")

    def share_link(self, filename):
        return f"https://dropbox.com/s/{filename}"


class CampusFTP:
    def connect(self):
        print("  FTP: connection opened")

    def put(self, filename, data):
        size = len(data)
        print(f"  FTP: PUT {filename} ({size} bytes)")

    def quit(self):
        print("  FTP: connection closed")

    def url(self, filename):
        return f"ftp://campus.edu/pub/{filename}"


# ---------- Target / Product ----------
class Storage(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def save(self, filename, content):
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def link(self, filename):
        pass


# ---------- Concrete Products, each one an Adapter ----------
class LocalDiskAdapter(Storage):                       # object adapter
    def __init__(self, adaptee):
        self.adaptee = adaptee

    def save(self, filename, content):
        self.adaptee.write(filename, content)

    def link(self, filename):
        return self.adaptee.path_of(filename)


class DropBoxAdapter(Storage):                         # object adapter
    def __init__(self, adaptee):
        self.adaptee = adaptee

    def save(self, filename, content):
        self.adaptee.upload_file(filename, content)

    def link(self, filename):
        return self.adaptee.share_link(filename)


class FtpAdapter(Storage):                             # object adapter
    def __init__(self, adaptee):
        self.adaptee = adaptee

    def save(self, filename, content):
        self.adaptee.connect()                         # one target call ->
        self.adaptee.put(filename, content)            # three adaptee calls
        self.adaptee.quit()

    def link(self, filename):
        return self.adaptee.url(filename)


# ---------- Creator ----------
class UploadService(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def create_storage(self):          # the factory method
        pass

    def store(self, filename, content):   # the template method
        storage = self.create_storage()
        print(f"Storing {filename}")
        storage.save(filename, content)
        location = storage.link(filename)
        print(f"  available at {location}\n")


# ---------- Concrete Creators ----------
class DevUploadService(UploadService):
    def create_storage(self):
        return LocalDiskAdapter(LocalDisk())


class CloudUploadService(UploadService):
    def create_storage(self):
        return DropBoxAdapter(DropBoxSDK())


class CampusUploadService(UploadService):
    def create_storage(self):
        return FtpAdapter(CampusFTP())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    services = [DevUploadService(), CloudUploadService(), CampusUploadService()]

    for service in services:
        service.store("thesis.pdf", "x" * 2048)

    void uploadFile(String filename, String blob) {
        int size = blob.length();
        System.out.println("  DropBox: uploaded " + filename + " (" + size + " bytes)");
    }

    String shareLink(String filename) {
        return "https://dropbox.com/s/" + filename;
    }
}

class CampusFTP {
    void connect() {
        System.out.println("  FTP: connection opened");
    }

    void put(String filename, String data) {
        int size = data.length();
        System.out.println("  FTP: PUT " + filename + " (" + size + " bytes)");
    }

    void quit() {
        System.out.println("  FTP: connection closed");
    }

    String url(String filename) {
        return "ftp://campus.edu/pub/" + filename;
    }
}

// ---------- Target / Product : ONE interface doing both jobs ----------
interface Storage {
    void save(String filename, String content);

    String link(String filename);
}

// ---------- Concrete Products, each one an Adapter ----------
class LocalDiskAdapter implements Storage {                 // object adapter
    private final LocalDisk adaptee;

    public LocalDiskAdapter(LocalDisk adaptee) {
        this.adaptee = adaptee;
    }

    @Override
    public void save(String filename, String content) {
        adaptee.write(filename, content);
    }

    @Override
    public String link(String filename) {
        return adaptee.pathOf(filename);
    }
}

class DropBoxAdapter implements Storage {                   // object adapter
    private final DropBoxSDK adaptee;

    public DropBoxAdapter(DropBoxSDK adaptee) {
        this.adaptee = adaptee;
    }

    @Override
    public void save(String filename, String content) {
        adaptee.uploadFile(filename, content);
    }

    @Override
    public String link(String filename) {
        return adaptee.shareLink(filename);
    }
}

class FtpAdapter implements Storage {                       // object adapter
    private final CampusFTP adaptee;

    public FtpAdapter(CampusFTP adaptee) {
        this.adaptee = adaptee;
    }

    @Override
    public void save(String filename, String content) {
        adaptee.connect();                // one target call ->
        adaptee.put(filename, content);   // three adaptee calls
        adaptee.quit();
    }

    @Override
    public String link(String filename) {
        return adaptee.url(filename);
    }
}

// ---------- Creator ----------
abstract class UploadService {
    protected abstract Storage createStorage();      // the factory method

    public void store(String filename, String content) {   // the template method
        Storage storage = createStorage();
        System.out.println("Storing " + filename);
        storage.save(filename, content);
        String location = storage.link(filename);
        System.out.println("  available at " + location + "\n");
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Creators ----------
class DevUploadService extends UploadService {
    @Override
    protected Storage createStorage() {
        return new LocalDiskAdapter(new LocalDisk());
    }
}

class CloudUploadService extends UploadService {
    @Override
    protected Storage createStorage() {
        return new DropBoxAdapter(new DropBoxSDK());
    }
}

class CampusUploadService extends UploadService {
    @Override
    protected Storage createStorage() {
        return new FtpAdapter(new CampusFTP());
    }
}

public class UploadDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        UploadService[] services = {
            new DevUploadService(), new CloudUploadService(), new CampusUploadService()
        };
        String content = "x".repeat(2048);

        for (UploadService service : services) {
            service.store("thesis.pdf", content);
        }
    }
}
