The overlap

The target interface and the product interface are the same type, and the adapters are the concrete products. The factory method can only stay clean because the adapters made three incompatible vendors substitutable for one another.

Marking points

  • No vendor class is edited. Any change there is an automatic deduction.
  • store takes only (filename, content) — no mode. If mode survives, the factory method was not applied, only decorated.
  • No vendor class name appears anywhere inside store, and no if/elif on a type string appears anywhere in the file.
  • create_storage is abstract on UploadService and overridden in each concrete creator.
  • All three adapters hold their vendor object in an adaptee field and call it — same shape three times, so the only thing that differs is the translation each one performs.
  • The three-call FTP sequence lives entirely inside FtpAdapter.save. If connect/quit leak into store, the target contract is broken — store would then be calling methods that only one of the three products has.
  • Driver treats all three services through the base type.
  • A common near-miss: writing the creators to return raw vendor objects and then adapting inside store. That puts the adaptation back in the shared routine and reintroduces the vendor vocabulary the adapter was supposed to remove. The creator must return something already conforming to Storage.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • "x".repeat(2048) needs Java 11+. Before that: new String(new char[2048]).replace('\0', 'x').
  • All three adapters keep their adaptee private, so connect, put and quit never reach the client. Written as a class adapter instead — FtpAdapter extends CampusFTP implements Storage — those four vendor methods would land on the adapter's own public surface, and a client holding an FtpAdapter could still call quit() directly. That difference in encapsulation, not the syntax, is the real argument for composition; Checkout with Two Payment Vendors puts the two forms side by side.
  • Because the creators are typed to return Storage, the compiler enforces the marking point about returning “something already conforming to the target” — a Java student physically cannot make the common near-miss without a cast.

Follow-up answers

1.Which fault in the given store did the adapter remove, and which did the factory method remove? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?

The adapter removed the vocabulary fault — store no longer knows that DropBox calls it upload_file or that FTP needs quit(). The factory method removed the selection fault — store no longer decides which back-end is built. Either alone leaves the other: adapters alone still leave an if/elif picking between them, and a factory alone still leaves store unable to call the products uniformly, because they share no interface to call.

2.The FTP adapter turns one call into three. Why is that the adapter's job and not the upload service's?

Because save is a promise the target interface makes to the client, and the client's routine must read identically for every back-end. Any vendor-specific sequencing is exactly what the adapter exists to hide. If store had to know FTP needs an open/close pair, every future back-end would force the shared routine to be edited again — the fault the whole exercise removes.

3.Google Drive is added next year, with yet another SDK. List exactly what you add and what you edit. Compare with the given code.

Two additions: a GoogleDriveAdapter product and a DriveUploadService creator. Nothing existing is edited — not store, not the other adapters, not the vendor SDKs. In the given code, store itself had to be reopened, and reopened for both reasons at once: a new branch in the chain and a new set of vendor method names inside it.

Combined patternsSingletonAdapter

The Card Reader

One scarce device, three modules

The story

The campus has one RFID card reader wired to one serial port. Several unrelated modules want to use it — the classroom attendance terminal, the library entry gate, the maintenance console — and none of them knows the others exist.

The hardware is genuinely scarce, and the vendor SDK enforces it: opening the port a second time throws a device error, because the licence permits a single live session. So there must be exactly one reader session for the whole campus, claimed the first time some module actually scans a card and not when the software boots.

The SDK is also nothing like what the modules want. It is vendor code you cannot edit. It talks in ports and raw hex tag numbers — 0xA31F0C — while every module wants one thing: give me the student ID of whoever just tapped their card. Right now each module opens the port itself, polls for a raw tag itself, and keeps its own copy of the tag-to-student lookup table. Three copies of the same translation, three attempts to claim a device that only one of them can have.

# ---- vendor SDK for the physical reader: DO NOT MODIFY ----
class RfidReaderSDK:
    _seat_taken = False          # the licence allows one live session
    _tags = ["0xA31F0C", "0xB77E21", "0xC10D45"]

    def __init__(self):
        self._cursor = 0

    def open_port(self, port):
        if RfidReaderSDK._seat_taken:
            raise RuntimeError("device error: port already in use by another session")
        RfidReaderSDK._seat_taken = True
        print(f"  RFID: port {port} opened, licence seat taken")

    def poll_raw(self):
        tag = RfidReaderSDK._tags[self._cursor % len(RfidReaderSDK._tags)]
        self._cursor += 1
        return tag

    def close_port(self):
        RfidReaderSDK._seat_taken = False
        print("  RFID: port closed")

CARD_TO_STUDENT = {
    "0xA31F0C": "21301001",
    "0xB77E21": "21301042",
    "0xC10D45": "21301117",
}

        self.room = room

    def take_attendance(self):
        reader = RfidReaderSDK()
        reader.open_port("COM3")
        raw = reader.poll_raw()
        print(f"[{self.room}] present: {CARD_TO_STUDENT.get(raw, 'UNKNOWN')}")

        reader.open_port("COM3")
        raw = reader.poll_raw()
        print(f"[Library] entry logged for {CARD_TO_STUDENT.get(raw, 'UNKNOWN')}")

import java.util.Map;

// ---- vendor SDK for the physical reader: DO NOT MODIFY ----
class RfidReaderSDK {
    private static boolean seatTaken = false;      // the licence allows one live session
    private static final String[] TAGS = {"0xA31F0C", "0xB77E21", "0xC10D45"};
    private int cursor = 0;

    void openPort(String port) {
        if (seatTaken) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("device error: port already in use by another session");
        }
        seatTaken = true;
        System.out.println("  RFID: port " + port + " opened, licence seat taken");
    }

    String pollRaw() {
        String tag = TAGS[cursor % TAGS.length];
        cursor++;
        return tag;
    }

    void closePort() {
        seatTaken = false;
        System.out.println("  RFID: port closed");
    }
}

// ---- your side: note the lookup table, copied into every module ----
class ClassroomTerminal {
    private static final Map<String, String> CARD_TO_STUDENT = Map.of(
            "0xA31F0C", "21301001",
            "0xB77E21", "21301042",
            "0xC10D45", "21301117");

    private final String room;

    ClassroomTerminal(String room) {
        this.room = room;
    }

    void takeAttendance() {
        RfidReaderSDK reader = new RfidReaderSDK();
        reader.openPort("COM3");
        String raw = reader.pollRaw();
        System.out.println("[" + room + "] present: "
                + CARD_TO_STUDENT.getOrDefault(raw, "UNKNOWN"));
    }
}

class LibraryGate {
    private static final Map<String, String> CARD_TO_STUDENT = Map.of(
            "0xA31F0C", "21301001",
            "0xB77E21", "21301042",
            "0xC10D45", "21301117");

    void admit() {
        RfidReaderSDK reader = new RfidReaderSDK();
        reader.openPort("COM3");
        String raw = reader.pollRaw();
        System.out.println("[Library] entry logged for "
                + CARD_TO_STUDENT.getOrDefault(raw, "UNKNOWN"));
    }
}

Read it first

Run this as given: the classroom terminal works, and the library gate crashes. That crash is the whole problem in one line.

Your task

  1. Declare the target interface — call it AttendanceScanner, with scan() returning a student ID string and status() returning a short readable state line. This is what every module should be written against; none of them should ever see a port, a raw tag, or the lookup table again.
  2. Adapt the vendor SDK to it. The port handling, the poll_raw call, and the hex-to-student-ID translation all move inside the adapter. The lookup table lives there too — exactly one copy.
  3. Make that one scanner object campus-wide. Every CardScannerAdapter() call must hand back the same object, created lazily, and the port must be opened exactly once — inside the same guard that creates the instance, so that claiming the device and creating the object cannot come apart.
  4. Rewrite the two modules to use the scanner instead of the SDK, and add a third — a MaintenanceConsole that never scans anything and only reports status(). It must reach the same live session as the other two.
  5. Add a release() that closes the port and lets a fresh session be claimed afterwards.
  6. Driver. Keep it short, but it must prove the design rather than merely exercise it: scan through at least two different modules, interleaved (the “port opened” line must appear exactly once for the whole run); have the maintenance console report a scan count that reflects scans made by the other modules; print an identity check, then release the reader.

Where this one goes wrong

__init__ runs on every call. If the adaptee is built there, the second module to scan will construct a fresh SDK object and hit the device error the story warns about.

How this one is judged

There is no fixed expected output for this problem. The test is simpler: if the port opens twice, or the maintenance console reports a count of zero, the design has not solved anything.

Follow-up questions (2–3 lines each)

Which fault in the given code did the adapter fix, and which did the singleton fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?
You used an object adapter here. Explain why the class adapter form — inheriting from RfidReaderSDK — sits badly with the singleton requirement in this particular problem.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Adaptee: vendor SDK for the physical reader, NOT modified ----------
class RfidReaderSDK:
    _seat_taken = False          # the licence allows one live session
    _tags = ["0xA31F0C", "0xB77E21", "0xC10D45"]

    def __init__(self):
        self._cursor = 0

    def open_port(self, port):
        if RfidReaderSDK._seat_taken:
            raise RuntimeError("device error: port already in use by another session")
        RfidReaderSDK._seat_taken = True
        print(f"  RFID: port {port} opened, licence seat taken")

    def poll_raw(self):
        tag = RfidReaderSDK._tags[self._cursor % len(RfidReaderSDK._tags)]
        self._cursor += 1
        return tag

    def close_port(self):
        RfidReaderSDK._seat_taken = False
        print("  RFID: port closed")


# ---------- Target ----------
class AttendanceScanner(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def scan(self):
        """returns a student ID string"""

    @abstractmethod
    def status(self):
        pass


# ---------- Adapter + Singleton ----------
class CardScannerAdapter(AttendanceScanner):
    _instance = None
    _CARD_TO_STUDENT = {
        "0xA31F0C": "21301001",
        "0xB77E21": "21301042",
        "0xC10D45": "21301117",
    }

    def __new__(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:                       # lazy creation
            print("Claiming the card reader...")
            cls._instance = super(CardScannerAdapter, cls).__new__(cls)
            cls._instance.adaptee = RfidReaderSDK()     # initialise ONCE, here
            cls._instance.adaptee.open_port("COM3")
            cls._instance.scan_count = 0
        return cls._instance

    def scan(self):
        raw = self.adaptee.poll_raw()                   # vendor vocabulary
        self.scan_count += 1
        return self._CARD_TO_STUDENT.get(raw, "UNKNOWN")

    def status(self):
        return f"reader ready, {self.scan_count} scan(s) this session"

    def release(self):
        self.adaptee.close_port()
        CardScannerAdapter._instance = None


# ---------- Clients: each one asks for a scanner independently ----------
class ClassroomTerminal:
    def __init__(self, room):
        self.room = room

    def take_attendance(self):
        student = CardScannerAdapter().scan()
        print(f"[{self.room}] present: {student}")


class LibraryGate:
    def admit(self):
        student = CardScannerAdapter().scan()
        print(f"[Library] entry logged for {student}")


class MaintenanceConsole:
    def report(self):
        status = CardScannerAdapter().status()
        print(f"[Maintenance] {status}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- campus opening, reader untouched ---")

    room = ClassroomTerminal("UB4-301")
    gate = LibraryGate()
    console = MaintenanceConsole()

    room.take_attendance()
    gate.admit()
    room.take_attendance()

    console.report()
    print("one scanner?", CardScannerAdapter() is CardScannerAdapter())

    CardScannerAdapter().release()

import java.util.Map;

// ---------- Adaptee: vendor SDK for the physical reader, NOT modified ----------
class RfidReaderSDK {
    private static boolean seatTaken = false;      // the licence allows one live session
    private static final String[] TAGS = {"0xA31F0C", "0xB77E21", "0xC10D45"};
    private int cursor = 0;

    void openPort(String port) {
        if (seatTaken) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("device error: port already in use by another session");
        }
        seatTaken = true;
        System.out.println("  RFID: port " + port + " opened, licence seat taken");
    }

    String pollRaw() {
        String tag = TAGS[cursor % TAGS.length];
        cursor++;
        return tag;
    }

    void closePort() {
        seatTaken = false;
        System.out.println("  RFID: port closed");
    }
}

// ---------- Target ----------
interface AttendanceScanner {
    String scan();                 // returns a student ID string

    String status();
}

// ---------- Adapter + Singleton ----------
class CardScannerAdapter implements AttendanceScanner {
    private static CardScannerAdapter instance;
    private static final Map<String, String> CARD_TO_STUDENT = Map.of(   // exactly one copy
            "0xA31F0C", "21301001",
            "0xB77E21", "21301042",
            "0xC10D45", "21301117");

    private final RfidReaderSDK adaptee;
    private int scanCount = 0;

    private CardScannerAdapter() {                        // claiming and creating cannot come apart
        System.out.println("Claiming the card reader...");
        this.adaptee = new RfidReaderSDK();
        this.adaptee.openPort("COM3");
    }

    public static CardScannerAdapter getInstance() {      // lazy creation
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new CardScannerAdapter();
        }
        return instance;
    }

    @Override
    public String scan() {
        String raw = adaptee.pollRaw();            // vendor vocabulary stops here
        scanCount++;
        return CARD_TO_STUDENT.getOrDefault(raw, "UNKNOWN");
    }

    @Override
    public String status() {
        return "reader ready, " + scanCount + " scan(s) this session";
    }

    public void release() {
        adaptee.closePort();
        instance = null;                           // let a fresh session be claimed
    }
}

// ---------- Clients: each one asks for a scanner independently ----------
class ClassroomTerminal {
    private final String room;

    public ClassroomTerminal(String room) {
        this.room = room;
    }

    public void takeAttendance() {
        String student = CardScannerAdapter.getInstance().scan();
        System.out.println("[" + room + "] present: " + student);
    }
}

class LibraryGate {
    public void admit() {
        String student = CardScannerAdapter.getInstance().scan();
        System.out.println("[Library] entry logged for " + student);
    }
}

class MaintenanceConsole {
    public void report() {
        String status = CardScannerAdapter.getInstance().status();
        System.out.println("[Maintenance] " + status);
    }
}

public class CardReaderDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("--- campus opening, reader untouched ---");

        ClassroomTerminal room = new ClassroomTerminal("UB4-301");
        LibraryGate gate = new LibraryGate();
        MaintenanceConsole console = new MaintenanceConsole();

        room.takeAttendance();
        gate.admit();
        room.takeAttendance();

        console.report();
        System.out.println("one scanner? "
                + (CardScannerAdapter.getInstance() == CardScannerAdapter.getInstance()));

        CardScannerAdapter.getInstance().release();
    }
}

Participants

RoleClass
AdapteeRfidReaderSDK
TargetAttendanceScanner
AdapterCardScannerAdapter
SingletonCardScannerAdapter
ClientsClassroomTerminal, LibraryGate, MaintenanceConsole

The overlap

CardScannerAdapter is doing two jobs at once — it translates the vendor's vocabulary into the target interface, and it guarantees that only one of it exists. It is the natural place for both, because it is the only class in the system that ever touches the device: if the wrapper is unique, the session is unique.

Marking points

  • The vendor SDK is not edited. Any change there is an automatic deduction — the scarcity check inside open_port is what makes the problem real.
  • open_port is called inside the __new__ guard, not in __init__ and not from a client. If the adaptee is constructed in __init__, the second CardScannerAdapter() call builds a fresh SDK and raises the device error — which is exactly the crash the story opens with, now moved somewhere less obvious. This is the trap.
  • _instance is a class attribute and the guard is if cls._instance is None, so the port opens on first scan, not at import.
  • The lookup table exists in exactly one place, inside the adapter. Three copies in three modules means task 2 was not done.
  • No client contains open_port, poll_raw, close_port, or a raw hex string.
  • MaintenanceConsole reports a non-zero scan count without ever scanning. That is the single best evidence the session is shared, and a driver that omits it should lose the task 6 mark.
  • release() closes the port and clears _instance, otherwise the next CardScannerAdapter() hands back a scanner whose port is shut. Students who close without clearing have built an object that lies about its state.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • The Python trap moves. In Java there is no __init__-runs-every-time hazard, so openPort sits safely in the private constructor. The Java version of the same mistake is a non-private constructor: leave it package-private and any module can still write new CardScannerAdapter(), claim a second seat and throw. Making the constructor private is what enforces the invariant.
  • instance = null inside release() assigns a static field from an instance method — legal, and worth flagging in review because it reads as if it only affects that object.
  • Map.of(...) builds an immutable map, so the shared lookup table cannot be mutated by a client that got hold of it. Python's class-level dict has no such protection.
  • The vendor's IllegalStateException is unchecked, so nothing forces a caller to handle it — the crash is a runtime surprise in both languages.

Follow-up answers

1.Which fault in the given code did the adapter fix, and which did the singleton fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?

The adapter fixed the vocabulary fault — modules asked for ports and hex tags when they wanted student IDs, and each kept its own translation table. The singleton fixed the scarcity fault — three modules each claiming a device that permits one session. Either alone leaves the other: an adapter without the singleton still lets every module construct its own adapter and crash on the second open_port; a singleton SDK without the adapter stops the crash but leaves all three modules parsing hex and duplicating the lookup table.

2.You used an object adapter here. Explain why the class adapter form — inheriting from RfidReaderSDK — sits badly with the singleton requirement in this particular problem.

A class adapter would inherit from RfidReaderSDK, so CardScannerAdapter is a reader — and every instantiation of it runs the vendor's __init__ and inherits open_port/close_port as part of its own public surface. That undermines both halves at once: the adapter can no longer hide the port lifecycle it was supposed to encapsulate, and clients can call close_port() directly on the shared singleton, shutting the session out from under every other module. Composition keeps the adaptee private, which is what a shared resource needs.

Combined patternsSingletonAdapter

The Campus SMS Gateway

The failure that never raises

The story

Several night jobs send SMS to students: the result publisher, the library overdue reminder, and an ops dashboard that only reports on what the others did. None of them knows the others exist.

They all go through one telecom gateway, and the licence permits one live session for the whole campus. The SDK does not refuse a second login — it does something worse. Authenticating again silently revokes the previous session, so the job that logged in first keeps running happily and every message it sends after that is quietly rejected. Nothing crashes. Students simply never receive their results.

The session must also not be claimed when the software boots — only the first time some job actually sends a message.

The SDK is vendor code you cannot edit, and it disagrees with your jobs on almost everything:

  • It only accepts batches, a list of dictionaries. Your jobs mostly want to send one message.
  • It wants numbers in international form — 8801712345678 — while campus records store the local form, 01712345678.
  • It reports outcomes as integer codes (0 delivered, 1 bad number, 3 revoked session), while your jobs want a plain true/false.
  • It hands back a session token that has to be carried into every later call.

Right now each job logs in for itself, converts its own numbers, wraps its own batch and reads the raw codes — which is both four copies of the same translation and the reason the sessions keep revoking each other.

class TeletalkBulkSMS:
    _live_token = None
    _issued = 0

        TeletalkBulkSMS._issued += 1
        TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token = f"SESS-{TeletalkBulkSMS._issued}"
        print(f"  gateway: session {TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token} issued "
              f"(any older session is now revoked)")
        return TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token

    def push_batch(self, token, entries):
        if token != TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token:
            print(f"  gateway: batch rejected, {token} was revoked")

                codes.append(0)

    def close_session(self, token):
        if token == TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token:
            TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token = None
            print(f"  gateway: {token} closed")

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

// ---- vendor SDK: DO NOT MODIFY ----
class TeletalkBulkSMS {
    private static String liveToken = null;
    private static int issued = 0;

    String authenticate(String apiKey) {
        issued++;
        liveToken = "SESS-" + issued;
        System.out.println("  gateway: session " + liveToken
                + " issued (any older session is now revoked)");
        return liveToken;
    }

    List<Integer> pushBatch(String token, List<Map<String, String>> entries) {
        List<Integer> codes = new ArrayList<>();
        if (!token.equals(liveToken)) {
            System.out.println("  gateway: batch rejected, " + token + " was revoked");
            for (int i = 0; i < entries.size(); i++) {
                codes.add(3);
            }
            return codes;
        }
        for (Map<String, String> entry : entries) {
            if (!entry.get("msisdn").startsWith("880")) {
                codes.add(1);
            } else {
                System.out.println("  gateway: -> " + entry.get("msisdn") + ": " + entry.get("body"));
                codes.add(0);
            }
        }
        return codes;
    }

    void closeSession(String token) {
        if (token.equals(liveToken)) {
            liveToken = null;
            System.out.println("  gateway: " + token + " closed");
        }
    }
}

Read it first

Run this as given, but construct both jobs before either one sends anything. The result publisher reports delivered: False and carries on as if nothing happened. No exception is raised anywhere. That silence is the fault you are fixing.

Your task

  1. Declare the target interface — call it SmsSender — with three methods: send(number, text) returning a single boolean, send_bulk(messages) taking a list of (number, text) pairs and returning a list of booleans, and status() returning a short readable line. Your jobs should never again see a token, a dictionary, an msisdn, or an integer code.
  2. Adapt the SDK to it. Four translations belong inside the adapter and nowhere else: local number to international form, single message to a batch of one, integer code to boolean, and carrying the session token. Implement send in terms of send_bulk rather than duplicating the work.
  3. Make the session campus-wide. Every CampusSmsAdapter() call must return the same object, created lazily, and authenticate must run exactly once — inside the same guard that creates the instance.
  4. Keep a running count of messages sent and failed, shared across all jobs, and report it through status().
  5. Rewrite the two jobs to use the target interface, and add a third — an OpsDashboard that sends nothing and only calls status().
  6. Add a release() that closes the session and allows a fresh one to be claimed later.
  7. Driver. Send through at least two different jobs, interleaved, and use send_bulk at least once with two recipients. The “session issued” line must appear exactly once. The ops dashboard must report a count covering messages sent by the other jobs. Print an identity check, then release the session.

Where this one goes wrong

__init__ runs on every call. If the SDK or the token is set up there, the second job to send a message re-authenticates and silently kills the first job's session — the original bug, moved somewhere harder to see.

How this one is judged

There is no fixed expected output. The test is: if a second session is ever issued, or the dashboard reports zero, the design has not solved anything — and note that neither failure will raise an exception, so you have to look.

Follow-up questions (2–3 lines each)

Which fault in the given code did the adapter fix, and which did the singleton fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?
send is written in terms of send_bulk. What would be lost if you implemented each separately, and what does that tell you about which of the two is the real adaptation?

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Adaptee: vendor SDK, NOT modified ----------
class TeletalkBulkSMS:
    _live_token = None
    _issued = 0

    def authenticate(self, api_key):
        TeletalkBulkSMS._issued += 1
        TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token = f"SESS-{TeletalkBulkSMS._issued}"
        print(f"  gateway: session {TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token} issued "
              f"(any older session is now revoked)")
        return TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token

    def push_batch(self, token, entries):
        if token != TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token:
            print(f"  gateway: batch rejected, {token} was revoked")
            return [3] * len(entries)
        codes = []
        for entry in entries:
            if not entry["msisdn"].startswith("880"):
                codes.append(1)
            else:
                print(f"  gateway: -> {entry['msisdn']}: {entry['body']}")
                codes.append(0)
        return codes

    def close_session(self, token):
        if token == TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token:
            TeletalkBulkSMS._live_token = None
            print(f"  gateway: {token} closed")


# ---------- Target ----------
class SmsSender(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def send(self, number, text):
        """one local number, returns True/False"""

    @abstractmethod
    def send_bulk(self, messages):
        """list of (number, text), returns list of True/False"""

    @abstractmethod
    def status(self):
        pass


# ---------- Adapter + Singleton ----------
class CampusSmsAdapter(SmsSender):
    _instance = None

    def __new__(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:                          # lazy creation
            print("Claiming the campus SMS session...")
            cls._instance = super(CampusSmsAdapter, cls).__new__(cls)
            cls._instance.adaptee = TeletalkBulkSMS()      # initialise ONCE, here
            cls._instance.token = cls._instance.adaptee.authenticate("campus-key")
            cls._instance.sent = 0
            cls._instance.failed = 0
        return cls._instance

    @staticmethod
    def _to_msisdn(local_number):                          # 017... -> 88017...
        return "88" + local_number.lstrip("+").replace(" ", "")

    def send(self, number, text):
        return self.send_bulk([(number, text)])[0]         # single -> batch of one

    def send_bulk(self, messages):
        entries = [{"msisdn": self._to_msisdn(n), "body": t} for n, t in messages]
        codes = self.adaptee.push_batch(self.token, entries)
        results = [code == 0 for code in codes]            # int code -> bool
        self.sent += results.count(True)
        self.failed += results.count(False)
        return results

    def status(self):
        return f"session live, {self.sent} sent / {self.failed} failed"

    def release(self):
        self.adaptee.close_session(self.token)
        CampusSmsAdapter._instance = None


# ---------- Clients ----------
class ResultPublisher:
    def notify(self, number, text):
        ok = CampusSmsAdapter().send(number, text)
        print(f"[Results] delivered: {ok}")


class LibraryOverdueJob:
    def remind_all(self, pairs):
        results = CampusSmsAdapter().send_bulk(pairs)
        delivered = results.count(True)
        total = len(results)
        print(f"[Library] {delivered} of {total} reminders delivered")


class OpsDashboard:
    def report(self):
        status = CampusSmsAdapter().status()
        print(f"[Ops] {status}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- night jobs starting, gateway untouched ---")

    results = ResultPublisher()
    library = LibraryOverdueJob()
    ops = OpsDashboard()

    results.notify("01712345678", "Spring result published")
    library.remind_all([("01812345678", "Book due tomorrow"),
                        ("01912345678", "Book overdue")])
    results.notify("01612345678", "Retake list published")

    ops.report()
    print("one session?", CampusSmsAdapter() is CampusSmsAdapter())

    CampusSmsAdapter().release()

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

// ---------- Adaptee: vendor SDK, NOT modified ----------
class TeletalkBulkSMS {
    private static String liveToken = null;
    private static int issued = 0;

    String authenticate(String apiKey) {
        issued++;
        liveToken = "SESS-" + issued;
        System.out.println("  gateway: session " + liveToken
                + " issued (any older session is now revoked)");
        return liveToken;
    }

    List<Integer> pushBatch(String token, List<Map<String, String>> entries) {
        List<Integer> codes = new ArrayList<>();
        if (!token.equals(liveToken)) {
            System.out.println("  gateway: batch rejected, " + token + " was revoked");
            for (int i = 0; i < entries.size(); i++) {
                codes.add(3);
            }
            return codes;
        }
        for (Map<String, String> entry : entries) {
            if (!entry.get("msisdn").startsWith("880")) {
                codes.add(1);
            } else {
                System.out.println("  gateway: -> " + entry.get("msisdn") + ": " + entry.get("body"));
                codes.add(0);
            }
        }
        return codes;
    }

    void closeSession(String token) {
        if (token.equals(liveToken)) {
            liveToken = null;
            System.out.println("  gateway: " + token + " closed");
        }
    }
}

// ---------- One outgoing message (Python used a plain tuple) ----------
class Message {
    final String number;
    final String text;

    Message(String number, String text) {
        this.number = number;
        this.text = text;
    }
}

// ---------- Target ----------
interface SmsSender {
    boolean send(String number, String text);           // one local number

    List<Boolean> sendBulk(List<Message> messages);

    String status();
}

// ---------- Adapter + Singleton ----------
class CampusSmsAdapter implements SmsSender {
    private static CampusSmsAdapter instance;

    private final TeletalkBulkSMS adaptee;
    private final String token;
    private int sent = 0;
    private int failed = 0;

    private CampusSmsAdapter() {                               // authenticates exactly once
        System.out.println("Claiming the campus SMS session...");
        this.adaptee = new TeletalkBulkSMS();
        this.token = adaptee.authenticate("campus-key");
    }

    public static CampusSmsAdapter getInstance() {             // lazy creation
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new CampusSmsAdapter();
        }
        return instance;
    }

    private static String toMsisdn(String localNumber) {          // 017... -> 88017...
        String clean = localNumber.replace(" ", "");
        if (clean.startsWith("+")) {
            clean = clean.substring(1);
        }
        return "88" + clean;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean send(String number, String text) {
        return sendBulk(List.of(new Message(number, text))).get(0);   // single -> batch of one
    }

    @Override
    public List<Boolean> sendBulk(List<Message> messages) {
        List<Map<String, String>> entries = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Message message : messages) {
            entries.add(Map.of("msisdn", toMsisdn(message.number), "body", message.text));
        }
        List<Integer> codes = adaptee.pushBatch(token, entries);
        List<Boolean> results = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int code : codes) {
            boolean ok = code == 0;                                   // int code -> boolean
            results.add(ok);
            if (ok) {
                sent++;
            } else {
                failed++;
            }
        }
        return results;
    }

    @Override
    public String status() {
        return "session live, " + sent + " sent / " + failed + " failed";
    }

    public void release() {
        adaptee.closeSession(token);
        instance = null;
    }
}

// ---------- Clients ----------
class ResultPublisher {
    public void notifyStudent(String number, String text) {
        boolean ok = CampusSmsAdapter.getInstance().send(number, text);
        System.out.println("[Results] delivered: " + ok);
    }
}

class LibraryOverdueJob {
    public void remindAll(List<Message> pairs) {
        List<Boolean> results = CampusSmsAdapter.getInstance().sendBulk(pairs);
        long delivered = results.stream().filter(ok -> ok).count();
        int total = results.size();
        System.out.println("[Library] " + delivered + " of " + total
                + " reminders delivered");
    }
}

class OpsDashboard {
    public void report() {
        String status = CampusSmsAdapter.getInstance().status();
        System.out.println("[Ops] " + status);
    }
}

public class CampusSmsDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("--- night jobs starting, gateway untouched ---");

        ResultPublisher results = new ResultPublisher();
        LibraryOverdueJob library = new LibraryOverdueJob();
        OpsDashboard ops = new OpsDashboard();

        results.notifyStudent("01712345678", "Spring result published");
        library.remindAll(List.of(new Message("01812345678", "Book due tomorrow"),
                                  new Message("01912345678", "Book overdue")));
        results.notifyStudent("01612345678", "Retake list published");

        ops.report();
        System.out.println("one session? "
                + (CampusSmsAdapter.getInstance() == CampusSmsAdapter.getInstance()));

        CampusSmsAdapter.getInstance().release();
    }
}

Demonstrating the fault first

Worth running in class before they start. Construct both jobs, then send. The result publisher reports False and continues. No exception, no stack trace — the messages are simply gone. This is the strongest version of the “it ran, so it works” lesson in the whole problem set.

  gateway: session SESS-1 issued (any older session is now revoked)
  gateway: session SESS-2 issued (any older session is now revoked)

Participants

RoleClass
AdapteeTeletalkBulkSMS
TargetSmsSender
AdapterCampusSmsAdapter
SingletonCampusSmsAdapter
ClientsResultPublisher, LibraryOverdueJob, OpsDashboard

The overlap

CampusSmsAdapter both translates the vendor's vocabulary into the target interface and guarantees only one of itself exists. It is the right place for both because it is the only class that ever holds a token — if the wrapper is unique, the session is unique.

Marking points

  • The vendor SDK is not edited. The revocation behaviour inside authenticate is what makes the problem real.
  • authenticate is called inside the __new__ guard. If the token, the SDK object or the counters are set up in __init__, that __init__ re-runs on every CampusSmsAdapter() call. Two things then go wrong, and neither raises: a fresh session is issued per call (seven session issued lines in the reference driver instead of one), and the counters reset, so OpsDashboard reports 0 sent / 0 failed. The messages still arrive — the shared instance means the new token overwrites the old one — and the identity check still prints True, so the output looks almost right. This is the trap, and the two driver tests in task 7 exist precisely to catch it.
  • _instance is a class attribute, guard is if cls._instance is None, so the session is claimed on first send rather than at import.
  • All four translations live in the adapter: "88" + number, single-to-batch, code == 0, and token carrying. Any of them appearing in a client means task 2 was not done.
  • No client contains authenticate, push_batch, msisdn, a raw dictionary, or an integer code comparison.
  • send delegates to send_bulk. Two independent implementations is a duplication smell — see follow-up 2.
  • Counters are updated in send_bulk only, so they stay correct however messages arrive.
  • OpsDashboard reports a non-zero count without sending anything. That is the best evidence the session is shared; a driver omitting it should lose the task 7 mark.
  • release() closes the session and clears _instance, otherwise the next CampusSmsAdapter() returns an object holding a dead token.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • Python's (number, text) tuple becomes a small Message class — or record Message(String number, String text) {} on Java 16+. Watch how much clearer List<Message> reads than the Python signature's implied “list of pairs”.
  • notify(String, String) would compile — it overloads Object.notify() rather than overriding it — but naming a method notify next to the observer problems in this set is asking for confusion, so the Java version uses notifyStudent.
  • token.equals(liveToken) inside the vendor SDK is null-safe in that direction; liveToken.equals(token) would throw once the session is closed. Objects.equals(a, b) sidesteps the question — a good habit to point at while it is visible.
  • The delivered flags print as true/false in Java and True/False in Python — the Output panel has tabs for both.
  • results.stream().filter(ok -> ok).count() returns a long, which is why the client prints long and int side by side. Python's results.count(True) hides the same distinction.

Follow-up answers

1.Which fault in the given code did the adapter fix, and which did the singleton fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?

The adapter fixed the vocabulary fault — batches, number formats, status codes and token plumbing repeated in every job. The singleton fixed the scarcity fault — one licensed session that jobs were revoking from one another. Either alone leaves the other: an adapter without the singleton lets each job build its own adapter, each authenticating and killing the last; a singleton SDK without the adapter stops the revocation but leaves every job converting numbers and reading integer codes by hand.

2.send is written in terms of send_bulk. What would be lost if you implemented each separately, and what does that tell you about which of the two is the real adaptation?

If implemented separately, the number conversion, the code-to-boolean mapping and the counter updates all exist twice and will drift the first time one is changed — the same DRY violation the lecture flags in the factory example, appearing here inside an adapter. It also hides which direction the adaptation runs: the vendor SDK is batch-only, so send_bulk is the real adaptation and send is a convenience built on top of it.

Combined patternsSingletonAdapter

The Currency Desk

Cost is the visible reason, consistency is the real one

The story

The finance office runs a nightly billing job for foreign-currency students. Three modules take part: tuition invoicing, scholarship disbursement, and a finance dashboard that issues no money and only reports on the run.

They all need exchange rates from a commercial provider, and every call to that provider is paid — the campus licence allows a handful per day, after which the call throws. So the rate table must be fetched once for the whole run and then reused, and it must not be fetched when the software boots — only the first time some module actually needs a rate.

There is a second reason, and it matters more than the money. Rates move during the night. If each module fetches its own table, two invoices issued minutes apart can be priced at different rates, and the books will not balance. Every figure in a single billing run must come from one table fetched at one moment.

The SDK is vendor code you cannot edit, and it does not speak the language the finance modules want:

  • It hands back the whole table as one CSV-ish string — USD:1.0,BDT:121.35,EUR:0.92,... — where the modules want a number for one specific pair.
  • Every rate in it is relative to USD. The modules mostly need BDT to something else, so the cross rate has to be worked out.
  • It needs a licence handshake first, and the resulting handle carried into every later call.

Right now each module connects for itself, fetches its own table, splits the string itself and works out its own cross rate — which is three copies of the same parsing code, three paid calls, and three snapshots of a moving market.

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

// ---- vendor SDK: DO NOT MODIFY ----
class FxRateService {
    static final int QUOTA = 3;
    private static int calls = 0;

    String connect(String licenceKey) {
        System.out.println("  fx: licence accepted");
        return "FX-HANDLE";
    }

    String fetchRates(String handle, String base) {
        if (calls >= QUOTA) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("fx error: daily quota exhausted");
        }
        calls++;
        System.out.println("  fx: rate table fetched, base " + base
                + " (paid call " + calls + "/" + QUOTA + ")");
        return "USD:1.0,BDT:121.35,EUR:0.92,GBP:0.79,JPY:157.10";
    }

    int callsUsed() {
        return calls;
    }
}

// ---- your side: the same twelve lines, copied three times ----
class TuitionInvoice {
    void issue(String student, int amountBdt, String currency) {
        FxRateService fx = new FxRateService();
        String handle = fx.connect("campus-licence");
        Map<String, Double> table = new HashMap<>();
        for (String pair : fx.fetchRates(handle, "USD").split(",")) {
            String[] kv = pair.split(":");
            table.put(kv[0], Double.parseDouble(kv[1]));
        }
        double converted = amountBdt * (table.get(currency) / table.get("BDT"));
        System.out.printf("[Invoice] %s: %d BDT = %.2f %s%n", student, amountBdt, converted, currency);
    }
}

class ScholarshipDisbursement {
    void pay(String student, int amountBdt, String currency) {
        FxRateService fx = new FxRateService();
        String handle = fx.connect("campus-licence");
        Map<String, Double> table = new HashMap<>();
        for (String pair : fx.fetchRates(handle, "USD").split(",")) {
            String[] kv = pair.split(":");
            table.put(kv[0], Double.parseDouble(kv[1]));
        }
        double converted = amountBdt * (table.get(currency) / table.get("BDT"));
        System.out.printf("[Scholarship] %s: %d BDT = %.2f %s%n", student, amountBdt, converted, currency);

}

class FinanceDashboard {
    void report(String currency) {
        FxRateService fx = new FxRateService();
        String handle = fx.connect("campus-licence");
        Map<String, Double> table = new HashMap<>();
        for (String pair : fx.fetchRates(handle, "USD").split(",")) {
            String[] kv = pair.split(":");
            table.put(kv[0], Double.parseDouble(kv[1]));
        }
        System.out.printf("[Finance] 1 %s = %.2f BDT%n",
                currency, table.get("BDT") / table.get(currency));

Read it first

Run this as given with two invoices, one scholarship and one dashboard report — four operations in all. Count the paid calls, and watch what happens on the fourth. Notice also that the dashboard is a module that issues no money at all, yet still burns a paid call just to report.

Your task

  1. Declare the target interface — call it RateProvider — with rate(from_ccy, to_ccy) returning a float, convert(amount, from_ccy, to_ccy) returning a rounded amount, and status() returning a short readable line. No finance module should ever again see a handle, a CSV string, or a division by a USD-based figure.
  2. Adapt the SDK to it. The licence handshake, the string parsing, the USD cross-rate arithmetic, and the rounding all belong inside the adapter and nowhere else. Implement convert in terms of rate rather than duplicating the arithmetic.
  3. Cache the table inside the adapter. fetch_rates must run exactly once for the run, with the parsed table kept for every later lookup.
  4. Make the desk campus-wide. Every CurrencyDeskAdapter() call must return the same object, created lazily, with the fetch happening inside the same guard that creates the instance — so the cache and the object cannot come apart.
  5. Track how many lookups the desk has served, across all modules, and report it through status() along with the number of paid calls used.
  6. Add a refresh() that deliberately spends one more paid call to replace the cached table, for the rare case where finance wants a mid-run re-price.
  7. Rewrite the three modules to use the target interface. The dashboard must be able to report without spending anything.
  8. Driver. Issue at least two invoices and one scholarship payment, through different modules. The “rate table fetched” line must appear exactly once, and the paid-call counter must still read 1 at the end. Two conversions of the same amount, made through two different modules, must produce identical figures. The dashboard must report a lookup count covering the other modules' work. Print an identity check.

Where this one goes wrong

__init__ runs on every call. If the fetch or the parsed table is set up there, every module re-fetches, the quota drains, and — before it drains — different modules quietly price their figures from different tables.

How this one is judged

There is no fixed expected output. The tests are: more than one paid call means the cache is not shared, and two equal amounts converting to different figures means the run is not consistent.

Follow-up questions (2–3 lines each)

Which fault in the given code did the adapter fix, and which did the singleton fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?
This problem gives two reasons for having one desk: cost and consistency. Which one would still justify the singleton if the provider were free and unlimited? Which is the stronger argument, and why?

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Adaptee: vendor SDK, NOT modified ----------
class FxRateService:
    QUOTA = 3
    _calls_used = 0

    def connect(self, licence_key):
        print("  fx: licence accepted")
        return "FX-HANDLE"

    def fetch_rates(self, handle, base):
        if FxRateService._calls_used >= FxRateService.QUOTA:
            raise RuntimeError("fx error: daily quota exhausted")
        FxRateService._calls_used += 1
        print(f"  fx: rate table fetched, base {base} "
              f"(paid call {FxRateService._calls_used}/{FxRateService.QUOTA})")
        return "USD:1.0,BDT:121.35,EUR:0.92,GBP:0.79,JPY:157.10"

    def calls_used(self):
        return FxRateService._calls_used


# ---------- Target ----------
class RateProvider(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def rate(self, from_ccy, to_ccy):
        """float, how many to_ccy one from_ccy buys"""

    @abstractmethod
    def convert(self, amount, from_ccy, to_ccy):
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def status(self):
        pass


# ---------- Adapter + Singleton ----------
class CurrencyDeskAdapter(RateProvider):
    _instance = None

    def __new__(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:                            # lazy creation
            print("Opening the currency desk for today...")
            cls._instance = super(CurrencyDeskAdapter, cls).__new__(cls)
            cls._instance.adaptee = FxRateService()          # initialise ONCE, here
            cls._instance.handle = cls._instance.adaptee.connect("campus-licence")
            cls._instance.table = cls._instance._load()
            cls._instance.lookups = 0
        return cls._instance

    def _load(self):
        raw = self.adaptee.fetch_rates(self.handle, "USD")   # one paid call
        table = {}
        for pair in raw.split(","):                          # CSV string -> floats
            code, value = pair.split(":")
            table[code] = float(value)
        return table

    def rate(self, from_ccy, to_ccy):
        self.lookups += 1
        return self.table[to_ccy] / self.table[from_ccy]     # cross rate via USD

    def convert(self, amount, from_ccy, to_ccy):
        return round(amount * self.rate(from_ccy, to_ccy), 2)

    def status(self):
        cached = len(self.table)
        used = self.adaptee.calls_used()
        return (f"{cached} currencies cached, {self.lookups} lookup(s) served, "
                f"{used}/{FxRateService.QUOTA} paid calls used")

    def refresh(self):
        self.table = self._load()                            # deliberate second call


# ---------- Clients ----------
class TuitionInvoice:
    def issue(self, student, amount_bdt, currency):
        converted = CurrencyDeskAdapter().convert(amount_bdt, "BDT", currency)
        print(f"[Invoice] {student}: {amount_bdt} BDT = {converted} {currency}")


class ScholarshipDisbursement:
    def pay(self, student, amount_bdt, currency):
        converted = CurrencyDeskAdapter().convert(amount_bdt, "BDT", currency)
        print(f"[Scholarship] {student}: {amount_bdt} BDT = {converted} {currency}")


class FinanceDashboard:
    def report(self):
        status = CurrencyDeskAdapter().status()
        print(f"[Finance] {status}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- billing run starting, no rates fetched yet ---")

    invoice = TuitionInvoice()
    scholarship = ScholarshipDisbursement()
    finance = FinanceDashboard()

    invoice.issue("Arif", 90000, "USD")
    invoice.issue("Mitu", 90000, "USD")
    scholarship.pay("Arif", 25000, "EUR")

    finance.report()
    print("one desk?", CurrencyDeskAdapter() is CurrencyDeskAdapter())

import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

// ---------- Adaptee: vendor SDK, NOT modified ----------
class FxRateService {
    static final int QUOTA = 3;
    private static int calls = 0;

    String connect(String licenceKey) {
        System.out.println("  fx: licence accepted");
        return "FX-HANDLE";
    }

    String fetchRates(String handle, String base) {
        if (calls >= QUOTA) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("fx error: daily quota exhausted");
        }
        calls++;
        System.out.println("  fx: rate table fetched, base " + base
                + " (paid call " + calls + "/" + QUOTA + ")");
        return "USD:1.0,BDT:121.35,EUR:0.92,GBP:0.79,JPY:157.10";
    }

    int callsUsed() {
        return calls;
    }
}

// ---------- Target ----------
interface RateProvider {
    double rate(String fromCcy, String toCcy);      // how many toCcy one fromCcy buys

    double convert(double amount, String fromCcy, String toCcy);

    String status();
}

// ---------- Adapter + Singleton ----------
class CurrencyDeskAdapter implements RateProvider {
    private static CurrencyDeskAdapter instance;

    private final FxRateService adaptee;
    private final String handle;
    private Map<String, Double> table;
    private int lookups = 0;

    private CurrencyDeskAdapter() {                             // fetch and instance cannot come apart
        System.out.println("Opening the currency desk for today...");
        this.adaptee = new FxRateService();
        this.handle = adaptee.connect("campus-licence");
        this.table = load();
    }

    public static CurrencyDeskAdapter getInstance() {           // lazy creation
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new CurrencyDeskAdapter();
        }
        return instance;
    }

    private Map<String, Double> load() {
        String raw = adaptee.fetchRates(handle, "USD");            // one paid call
        Map<String, Double> parsed = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        for (String pair : raw.split(",")) {                       // CSV string -> doubles
            String[] kv = pair.split(":");
            parsed.put(kv[0], Double.parseDouble(kv[1]));
        }
        return parsed;
    }

    @Override
    public double rate(String fromCcy, String toCcy) {
        lookups++;
        return table.get(toCcy) / table.get(fromCcy);              // cross rate via USD
    }

    @Override
    public double convert(double amount, String fromCcy, String toCcy) {
        return Math.round(amount * rate(fromCcy, toCcy) * 100.0) / 100.0;
    }

    @Override
    public String status() {
        int cached = table.size();
        int used = adaptee.callsUsed();
        return cached + " currencies cached, " + lookups + " lookup(s) served, "
                + used + "/" + FxRateService.QUOTA + " paid calls used";
    }

    public void refresh() {
        this.table = load();                                       // deliberate second call
    }
}

// ---------- Clients ----------
class TuitionInvoice {
    public void issue(String student, int amountBdt, String currency) {
        double converted = CurrencyDeskAdapter.getInstance().convert(amountBdt, "BDT", currency);
        System.out.println("[Invoice] " + student + ": " + amountBdt
                + " BDT = " + converted + " " + currency);
    }
}

class ScholarshipDisbursement {
    public void pay(String student, int amountBdt, String currency) {
        double converted = CurrencyDeskAdapter.getInstance().convert(amountBdt, "BDT", currency);
        System.out.println("[Scholarship] " + student + ": " + amountBdt
                + " BDT = " + converted + " " + currency);
    }
}

class FinanceDashboard {
    public void report() {
        String status = CurrencyDeskAdapter.getInstance().status();
        System.out.println("[Finance] " + status);
    }
}

public class CurrencyDeskDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("--- billing run starting, no rates fetched yet ---");

        TuitionInvoice invoice = new TuitionInvoice();
        ScholarshipDisbursement scholarship = new ScholarshipDisbursement();
        FinanceDashboard finance = new FinanceDashboard();

        invoice.issue("Arif", 90000, "USD");
        invoice.issue("Mitu", 90000, "USD");
        scholarship.pay("Arif", 25000, "EUR");

        finance.report();
        System.out.println("one desk? "
                + (CurrencyDeskAdapter.getInstance() == CurrencyDeskAdapter.getInstance()));
    }
}

Participants

RoleClass
AdapteeFxRateService
TargetRateProvider
AdapterCurrencyDeskAdapter
SingletonCurrencyDeskAdapter
ClientsTuitionInvoice, ScholarshipDisbursement, FinanceDashboard

The overlap

CurrencyDeskAdapter translates the vendor's vocabulary into the target interface and guarantees only one of itself exists. Here the second job has a consequence the earlier problems did not have — the singleton is also what makes the cache shared. One wrapper means one table, which means one paid call and one consistent set of figures.

Marking points

  • The vendor SDK is not edited. The quota check inside fetch_rates is what makes the problem real.
  • connect and fetch_rates are called inside the __new__ guard. If the fetch happens in __init__, every CurrencyDeskAdapter() call re-fetches: the quota drains after three modules, and — more seriously — figures produced before the drain come from different tables. This is the trap.
  • _instance is a class attribute, guard is if cls._instance is None, so nothing is fetched at import.
  • Parsing, the cross-rate division, the handle, and the rounding all live in the adapter. Any of them appearing in a finance module means task 2 was not done.
  • No client contains connect, fetch_rates, split(","), or a division by table["BDT"].
  • convert delegates to rate. Two independent implementations of the arithmetic is a duplication smell.
  • refresh() re-fetches and replaces the table, without creating a second instance. A refresh that clears _instance would let the old desk's users keep a stale table — check for that.
  • The dashboard reports a non-zero lookup count while spending nothing. Best single piece of evidence the desk is shared; a driver omitting it should lose the task 8 mark.
  • Two conversions of 90000 BDT through two different modules must print the same figure to the last decimal.

Java notes — where the translation is not one-to-one

  • Python's round(x, 2) and Java's Math.round(x * 100.0) / 100.0 agree here, but they are not the same function: Python 3 uses banker's rounding (round(2.5) is 2), Java rounds half up. On money, neither is really right — BigDecimal with an explicit RoundingMode is.
  • LinkedHashMap rather than HashMap so status() and any future dump list currencies in the order the vendor sent them. Python dicts have kept insertion order since 3.7, which is why the Python version needs no equivalent choice.
  • table is not final — refresh() replaces it. Everything else in the desk is final, which is a useful signal in review: the one mutable field is the one thing that is meant to change.
  • The vendor's calls counter is static, so it survives refresh() and any new instance — which is exactly why the quota is a global budget and no amount of object juggling on your side escapes it.

Follow-up answers

1.Which fault in the given code did the adapter fix, and which did the singleton fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?

The adapter fixed the vocabulary fault — a CSV string, a USD-relative table and a licence handle, re-parsed in every module. The singleton fixed the shared resource fault — one paid quota and one cached snapshot. Either alone leaves the other: an adapter without the singleton has every module building its own desk, fetching its own table and blowing the quota; a shared SDK object without the adapter stops the extra calls but leaves three copies of the parsing and cross-rate code, which is where a rounding or direction bug will eventually differ between modules.

2.This problem gives two reasons for having one desk: cost and consistency. Which one would still justify the singleton if the provider were free and unlimited? Which is the stronger argument, and why?

Consistency survives a free, unlimited provider — rates move whether or not calls are billed, so a run that fetches twice can still price two invoices differently. That makes it the stronger argument: cost is a budget problem that a bigger licence solves, while inconsistency is a correctness problem that no licence fixes. A good answer notices that the money is the visible reason and the consistency is the real one.

Combined patternsSingletonFactory Method

IT Helpdesk Tickets

Collaboration, not overlap

The story

The university IT helpdesk runs three desks: hardware, software and network. Each desk raises a different kind of ticket — they carry different response deadlines and print differently — but every desk follows the exact same routine when a complaint arrives: take a tracking number, create the ticket, file it, and tell the reporter the deadline. That routine never changes. What changes is which kind of ticket a given desk produces. A desk knows when a ticket must be created, not what kind.

Cutting across all three desks is the ticket log. There must be exactly one log for the whole helpdesk, because it does two jobs that only work if nothing is duplicated:

  • It issues the tracking numbers, in one unbroken sequence. TKT-0001, TKT-0002, TKT-0003 — and a number must never be handed out twice, no matter which desk asked for it.
  • It holds every ticket raised today, so the supervisor's console — which raises no tickets of its own and belongs to no desk — can list all of them at the end of the shift.

The log must also not open when the helpdesk software boots; it should be created the first time some desk actually needs a number.

class TicketRegistry:
    def __init__(self):
        print("Opening ticket log for today...")
        self.counter = 0
        self.tickets = []

    def next_id(self):
        self.counter += 1
        return f"TKT-{self.counter:04d}"

    def record(self, ticket):
        self.tickets.append(ticket)

    def summary(self):
        print(f"\n{len(self.tickets)} ticket(s) on file")
        for ticket in self.tickets:
            print(f"  {ticket.ticket_id} {ticket.describe()}")


class HardwareTicket:
    def __init__(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        self.ticket_id = ticket_id
        self.reporter = reporter

    def sla_hours(self):
        return 24

    def describe(self):
        return f"[HARDWARE] reported by {self.reporter}"


class SoftwareTicket:
    def __init__(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        self.ticket_id = ticket_id
        self.reporter = reporter

    def sla_hours(self):
        return 8

    def describe(self):
        return f"[SOFTWARE] reported by {self.reporter}"


class NetworkTicket:
    def __init__(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        self.ticket_id = ticket_id
        self.reporter = reporter

    def sla_hours(self):
        return 2

    def describe(self):
        return f"[NETWORK] reported by {self.reporter}"


class TicketDesk:
    def open_ticket(self, kind, reporter):
        registry = TicketRegistry()
        ticket_id = registry.next_id()
        if kind == "hardware":
            ticket = HardwareTicket(ticket_id, reporter)
        elif kind == "software":
            ticket = SoftwareTicket(ticket_id, reporter)
        else:
            ticket = NetworkTicket(ticket_id, reporter)
        registry.record(ticket)
        print(f"{ticket_id} opened - {ticket.describe()}, "
              f"resolve within {ticket.sla_hours()}h")


class SupervisorConsole:
    def review(self):
        registry = TicketRegistry()
        registry.summary()

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

class TicketRegistry {
    int counter;
    List<Object> tickets;

    TicketRegistry() {
        System.out.println("Opening ticket log for today...");
        this.counter = 0;
        this.tickets = new ArrayList<>();
    }

    String nextId() {
        counter++;
        return String.format("TKT-%04d", counter);
    }

    void record(Object ticket) {
        tickets.add(ticket);
    }

    void summary() {
        System.out.println("\n" + tickets.size() + " ticket(s) on file");
        for (Object ticket : tickets) {
            // no common type: the log cannot even print itself without
            // asking each ticket what it happens to be
            if (ticket instanceof HardwareTicket t) {
                System.out.println("  " + t.ticketId + " " + t.describe());
            } else if (ticket instanceof SoftwareTicket t) {
                System.out.println("  " + t.ticketId + " " + t.describe());
            } else if (ticket instanceof NetworkTicket t) {
                System.out.println("  " + t.ticketId + " " + t.describe());
            }
        }
    }
}

class HardwareTicket {
    String ticketId;
    String reporter;

    HardwareTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        this.ticketId = ticketId;
        this.reporter = reporter;
    }

    int slaHours() {
        return 24;
    }

    String describe() {
        return "[HARDWARE] reported by " + reporter;
    }
}

class SoftwareTicket {
    String ticketId;
    String reporter;

    SoftwareTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        this.ticketId = ticketId;
        this.reporter = reporter;
    }

    int slaHours() {
        return 8;
    }

    String describe() {
        return "[SOFTWARE] reported by " + reporter;
    }
}

class NetworkTicket {
    String ticketId;
    String reporter;

    NetworkTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        this.ticketId = ticketId;
        this.reporter = reporter;
    }

    int slaHours() {
        return 2;
    }

    String describe() {
        return "[NETWORK] reported by " + reporter;
    }
}

class TicketDesk {
    void openTicket(String kind, String reporter) {
        TicketRegistry registry = new TicketRegistry();
        String ticketId = registry.nextId();
        if (kind.equals("hardware")) {
            HardwareTicket ticket = new HardwareTicket(ticketId, reporter);
            registry.record(ticket);
            System.out.println(ticketId + " opened - " + ticket.describe()
                    + ", resolve within " + ticket.slaHours() + "h");
        } else if (kind.equals("software")) {
            SoftwareTicket ticket = new SoftwareTicket(ticketId, reporter);
            registry.record(ticket);
            System.out.println(ticketId + " opened - " + ticket.describe()
                    + ", resolve within " + ticket.slaHours() + "h");
        } else {
            NetworkTicket ticket = new NetworkTicket(ticketId, reporter);
            registry.record(ticket);
            System.out.println(ticketId + " opened - " + ticket.describe()
                    + ", resolve within " + ticket.slaHours() + "h");
        }
    }
}

class SupervisorConsole {
    void review() {
        TicketRegistry registry = new TicketRegistry();
        registry.summary();
    }
}

Read it first

Run this as it stands and watch what the tracking numbers do across two desks, then watch what the supervisor's console reports. Both faults come from the same cause.

Your task

  1. Guarantee one registry. Every TicketRegistry() call must hand back the same object, created lazily. TicketDesk and SupervisorConsole must keep calling TicketRegistry() exactly as they do now — you may not edit them to receive the registry as an argument.
  2. Give the three ticket classes a common product interface with sla_hours() and describe(). Lift the shared __init__ into it.
  3. Turn TicketDesk into the creator. open_ticket keeps the shared routine, but the ticket it files comes from an abstract factory method. open_ticket must no longer take a kind argument, and no concrete ticket class name may appear inside it.
  4. Write one concrete creator per desk — HardwareDesk, SoftwareDesk, NetworkDesk. The if/elif chain must disappear completely.
  5. Driver. Open at least four tickets through at least three different desks, interleaved — not all the hardware ones first. The printed tracking numbers must form one unbroken sequence with no repeat, which is only possible if the registry is shared. Then call the supervisor's console, which belongs to no desk, and show it can see every ticket raised. Print an identity check on the registry.

Where this one goes wrong

__init__ runs on every call. If the counter or the ticket list is initialised in the wrong place, every desk silently resets the sequence back to zero.

How this one is judged

There is no fixed expected output for this problem — but if two desks ever issue the same number, or the supervisor sees fewer tickets than were opened, your registry is not doing its job.

Follow-up questions (2–3 lines each)

Which fault in the given code did the singleton fix, and which did the factory method fix? Could you have applied either one alone? What would still be wrong?
A fourth desk for printer complaints opens next semester. List exactly what you add and what you edit. Compare with the given code.

Part B (optional, for those who finish early)

Each desk object holds no state of its own, so the helpdesk wonders whether every desk should be a singleton too — one HardwareDesk object, one SoftwareDesk object, and so on.

Try it. Put the singleton machinery on the shared TicketDesk base class so all three inherit it, and predict before you run it: does each desk get its own single instance, or do all three collapse into one? Then write the guard a second way — once as if cls._instance is None and once as if TicketDesk._instance is None — and explain why the two behave differently. One line of the Python data model accounts for the whole difference.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ---------- Singleton ----------
class TicketRegistry:
    _instance = None

    def __new__(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:                      # lazy creation
            print("Opening ticket log for today...")
            cls._instance = super(TicketRegistry, cls).__new__(cls)
            cls._instance._counter = 0                 # initialise ONCE, here
            cls._instance._tickets = []
        return cls._instance

    def next_id(self):
        self._counter += 1
        return f"TKT-{self._counter:04d}"

    def record(self, ticket):
        self._tickets.append(ticket)

    def summary(self):
        count = len(self._tickets)
        print(f"\n{count} ticket(s) on file")
        for ticket in self._tickets:
            description = ticket.describe()
            print(f"  {ticket.ticket_id} {description}")


# ---------- Product ----------
class Ticket(ABC):
    def __init__(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        self.ticket_id = ticket_id
        self.reporter = reporter

    @abstractmethod
    def sla_hours(self):
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def describe(self):
        pass


# ---------- Concrete Products ----------
class HardwareTicket(Ticket):
    def sla_hours(self):
        return 24

    def describe(self):
        return f"[HARDWARE] reported by {self.reporter}"


class SoftwareTicket(Ticket):
    def sla_hours(self):
        return 8

    def describe(self):
        return f"[SOFTWARE] reported by {self.reporter}"


class NetworkTicket(Ticket):
    def sla_hours(self):
        return 2

    def describe(self):
        return f"[NETWORK] reported by {self.reporter}"


# ---------- Creator ----------
class TicketDesk(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def create_ticket(self, ticket_id, reporter):      # the factory method
        pass

    def open_ticket(self, reporter):                   # the template method
        registry = TicketRegistry()
        ticket_id = registry.next_id()
        ticket = self.create_ticket(ticket_id, reporter)
        registry.record(ticket)
        description = ticket.describe()
        sla = ticket.sla_hours()
        print(f"{ticket_id} opened - {description}, resolve within {sla}h")
        return ticket


# ---------- Concrete Creators ----------
class HardwareDesk(TicketDesk):
    def create_ticket(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        return HardwareTicket(ticket_id, reporter)


class SoftwareDesk(TicketDesk):
    def create_ticket(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        return SoftwareTicket(ticket_id, reporter)


class NetworkDesk(TicketDesk):
    def create_ticket(self, ticket_id, reporter):
        return NetworkTicket(ticket_id, reporter)


# ---------- A client that never creates a ticket ----------
class SupervisorConsole:
    def review(self):
        TicketRegistry().summary()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- helpdesk opening, log not touched yet ---")

    hardware = HardwareDesk()
    software = SoftwareDesk()
    network = NetworkDesk()

    hardware.open_ticket("Nabil")
    software.open_ticket("Sadia")
    network.open_ticket("Rafi")
    software.open_ticket("Tanha")

    SupervisorConsole().review()
    print("\none registry?", TicketRegistry() is TicketRegistry())

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

// ---------- Singleton ----------
class TicketRegistry {
    private static TicketRegistry instance;
    private int counter = 0;
    private final List<Ticket> tickets = new ArrayList<>();

    private TicketRegistry() {
        System.out.println("Opening ticket log for today...");
    }

    public static TicketRegistry getInstance() {          // lazy creation
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new TicketRegistry();
        }
        return instance;
    }

    public String nextId() {
        counter++;
        return String.format("TKT-%04d", counter);
    }

    public void record(Ticket ticket) {
        tickets.add(ticket);
    }

    public void summary() {
        int count = tickets.size();
        System.out.println("\n" + count + " ticket(s) on file");
        for (Ticket ticket : tickets) {
            String description = ticket.describe();
            System.out.println("  " + ticket.getTicketId() + " " + description);
        }
    }
}

// ---------- Product ----------
abstract class Ticket {
    private final String ticketId;
    private final String reporter;

    protected Ticket(String ticketId, String reporter) {   // the shared constructor
        this.ticketId = ticketId;
        this.reporter = reporter;
    }

    public String getTicketId() {
        return ticketId;
    }

    public String getReporter() {
        return reporter;
    }

    public abstract int slaHours();

    public abstract String describe();
}

// ---------- Concrete Products ----------
class HardwareTicket extends Ticket {
    public HardwareTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        super(ticketId, reporter);
    }

    @Override
    public int slaHours() {
        return 24;
    }

    @Override
    public String describe() {
        return "[HARDWARE] reported by " + getReporter();
    }
}

class SoftwareTicket extends Ticket {
    public SoftwareTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        super(ticketId, reporter);
    }

    @Override
    public int slaHours() {
        return 8;
    }

    @Override
    public String describe() {
        return "[SOFTWARE] reported by " + getReporter();
    }
}

class NetworkTicket extends Ticket {
    public NetworkTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        super(ticketId, reporter);
    }

    @Override
    public int slaHours() {
        return 2;
    }

    @Override
    public String describe() {
        return "[NETWORK] reported by " + getReporter();
    }
}

// ---------- Creator ----------
abstract class TicketDesk {
    protected abstract Ticket createTicket(String ticketId, String reporter);  // the factory method

    public Ticket openTicket(String reporter) {                // the template method
        TicketRegistry registry = TicketRegistry.getInstance();   // <- the two patterns meet here
        String ticketId = registry.nextId();
        Ticket ticket = createTicket(ticketId, reporter);
        registry.record(ticket);
        String description = ticket.describe();
        int slaHours = ticket.slaHours();
        System.out.println(ticketId + " opened - " + description
                + ", resolve within " + slaHours + "h");
        return ticket;
    }
}

// ---------- Concrete Creators ----------
class HardwareDesk extends TicketDesk {
    @Override
    protected Ticket createTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        return new HardwareTicket(ticketId, reporter);
    }
}

class SoftwareDesk extends TicketDesk {
    @Override
    protected Ticket createTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        return new SoftwareTicket(ticketId, reporter);
    }
}

class NetworkDesk extends TicketDesk {
    @Override
    protected Ticket createTicket(String ticketId, String reporter) {
        return new NetworkTicket(ticketId, reporter);
    }
}

// ---------- A client that never creates a ticket ----------
class SupervisorConsole {
    public void review() {
        TicketRegistry.getInstance().summary();
    }
}

public class HelpdeskDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("--- helpdesk opening, log not touched yet ---");

        TicketDesk hardware = new HardwareDesk();
        TicketDesk software = new SoftwareDesk();
        TicketDesk network = new NetworkDesk();

        hardware.openTicket("Nabil");
        software.openTicket("Sadia");
        network.openTicket("Rafi");
        software.openTicket("Tanha");

        new SupervisorConsole().review();
        System.out.println("\none registry? "
                + (TicketRegistry.getInstance() == TicketRegistry.getInstance()));
    }
}
